articles.title: Week 12 Fantasy Football Sleepers: Chris Rodriguez Jr., Antonio Williams among underrated options off the waiver wire
articles.summary: Scott Pianowski shares some potential sleepers you can find on the fantasy football waiver wire for Week 12.
articles.body:
Cam Ward and Justice Hill were winners for the sleeper page last week, not a bad ratio given how deep we dig. Let's try to keep the good vibes flowing in Week 12.

Keep in mind with this slate, all 32 NFL teams are in action. Hopefully your teams aren't crushed with injuries and you can play the hits here — roll with your best players, the widely-rostered guys. But shrewd fantasy managers know it's important to stay open-minded and keep working the waiver wire, even if you're just improving your depth or keeping a useful player out of the hands of your opponents.

WR Antonio Williams at Cardinals (46%) : Williams got off to a slow start Monday, dodging raindrops, but he was an undeniable monster in the late stages of the game, posting a 9-122-0 line against the Bengals. The Commanders face Arizona and Tennessee the next two weeks, teams that have not defended the pass well all year. Jayden Daniels has full trust in Williams now, and fantasy managers aren't far behind.

RB Chris Rodriguez Jr. vs. Titans (39%) : If Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) isn't able to play, Rodriguez is an easy start against a Tennessee defense that's fallen apart in recent weeks. And even if Tuten does start, the Jaguars still might want Rodriguez handling the clock-killing work, a likely game script given that the Jaguars are 14.5-point favorites.

RB Samaje Perine vs. Saints (33%) : He's been more efficient than Chase Brown in recent weeks, and with that, the role is expanding — Perine has 31 touches over three games. The Saints are the third-best matchup for opposing running backs, so if your backfield is riddled by injuries, Perine is a possible solution. His excellent pass-blocking endears him to coaching staffs, and he's always been a capable receiver.

WR Ted Hurst III vs. Panthers (2%) : The Hurst sleeper case went cold back in Week 9, when he saw just one offensive snap (a drop) and was mothballed after that. But the Buccaneers went back to Hurst after the bye and he was the team's best receiver at Detroit (5-56-2). With Emeka Egbuka slumping and Chris Godwin Jr. likely on his final lap, Hurst at least makes sense as a depth addition.

QB Deshaun Watson vs. Raiders (23%) : Watson's career looked all but finished when the year started, but Todd Monken's creative scheming and a bunch of talented pass-catches have brought the story back to life. Watson has 300-plus passing yards in his last three starts, and he's also starting to run proactively again, like he did in Houston. The remainder of the schedule is favorable, starting with a home date against the Raiders on Sunday night.

TE Pat Freiermuth vs. Broncos (36%) : He was used more in last week's loss, securing five passes, and it's possible the Mason Rudolph appointment will give the Steelers some juice in the passing game. Denver's outside corners are among the best in the game, but tight ends have been beating the Broncos down the seam all season. Keep the light on for Freiermuth.

Editor's note: Analysis included prior to Wednesday's Packers-Rams matchup

WR Konata Mumpfield vs. Packers (19%) : The Rams are missing tons of key personnel in the passing game, and it's possible they'll let Kyren Williams and Blake Corum dominate the touches Wednesday night. But Sean McVay isn't likely to play 1977 football entirely, and Mumpfield did manage a useful 3-81-0 line from his last start, though he only saw four targets.

articles.title: West Ham: Why Scott Parker is struggling to halt the slide after inheriting a host of problems
articles.summary: West Ham on course for lowest finish since 1957 following six-game winless streak; Scott Parker unable to arrest slide of side accused of lacking leaders and character following Premier League relegation last season
articles.body:
There was a sense that, had Nuno Espirito Santo been given more time, he might have kept West Ham in the Premier League. After all, 25 points from the final 17 games of the season suggested he was beginning to steady the ship and that, with a little longer, he could have turned things around.

Yet another 17 games later, Nuno is out of a job, while Scott Parker - a man who metaphorically bleeds claret and blue and boasts a formidable record in the Championship - has so far failed to make the anticipated impact as his replacement.

The Hammers have not finished a season outside the top half of the second tier for 71 years. However, an unbalanced squad and a dressing room increasingly feeling the pressure have fuelled fears that this remarkable record could finally come to an end this season - for the first time since the days of the Suez Crisis.

There is no question a squad boasting England winger Jarrod Bowen, Czech Republic stalwart Tomas Soucek and a number of other seasoned top-flight and established international players should be doing far better than 13th in the table and 11 points off the top.

But the logic behind West Ham's plight goes far beyond technical ability. They are among the slowest starters in the Championship and, despite losing only five games, have conceded first in 10 separate matches - second only to basement side Derby.

The Hammers need to play their way into games, both conceding a league-high and scoring a league-low proportion of their goals before half-time.

In a young dressing room, featuring nine players aged 21 or under, there have been justified questions over the lack of leaders beyond Bowen and, more damningly, a perceived lack of character - something Parker has himself felt the need to address from the touchline, having so far failed to arrest the slide that cost Nuno his job.

He recently told TalkSport : "You're coming out of the Premier League, the lights and the big stadiums and the clubs you play against.

"Then all of a sudden you have the big change of playing the Championship with certain habits and things you need to be. It's key in understanding that, and if there's a player here playing in this division at this moment in time, it's because it is what it is.

"We need to show the best versions of ourselves if we're going to get out of this division."

If anyone knows what it takes to do exactly that it is Parker, having achieved three promotions with three different clubs across as many seasons in the second tier.

In all of those three previous roles, he enjoyed the holy grail of a pre-season with his squad. But there is no such time to learn and tweak at the London Stadium, where the former England midfielder was thrust into his first competitive game at Cardiff only 12 hours after taking the job.

That would be challenging enough, but with the sheer number of issues Parker has to address, he has faced more spinning plates than he can handle at once in his first weeks in the role.

The Hammers are comfortably the Championship's highest scorers with their issues largely at the other end of the pitch, and frustration which has begun to spill over into the stands.

Goalkeeper Mads Hermansen has been dropped after drawing the ire of the home support, with homegrown replacement Finlay Herrick an obvious crowd favourite but struggling to adapt to the physical demands of the Championship. He was also largely at fault for Preston's opener from a corner last weekend.

Max Kilman's nightmare spell in east London has continued in the absence of Axel Disasi, who was unwilling to drop down to the Championship and turn his loan spell permanent in the summer after playing a major part in the Hammers' upturn last season.

There have been calls for Nottingham Forest loanee Morato to take his place, but nine of his 10 starts this season have come at left-back. The Hammers are also monitoring the situation of Man Utd defender Ayden Heaven , with the 20-year-old open to leaving Old Trafford in January.

But even in attack, things have begun to dry up. West Ham drew a blank for the first time all season in Tuesday night's 1-0 reverse at Portsmouth, after a toothless draw with Preston in their previous game.

It is far from conclusive proof, but the Hammers appear to miss January signing Pablo, who has been conspicuous by his absence from every matchday squad since Parker's arrival. West Ham picked up 13 points from the six games he started this season, despite the 22-year-old scoring just once.

There are also growing questions over the reasons behind his mysterious exile, adding to a wider sense of unease at the London Stadium which Parker must find a solution to sooner rather than later.

It is still barely two years since West Ham were playing in the Europa League quarter-finals and finishing ninth in the Premier League. Right now, however, that feels a lifetime ago.

articles.body:

Oliver Glasner's Nottingham Forest side are 17th in the table and outside the relegation zone on goal difference. But in their last home game they emphatically beat Manchester City 3-1 , thanks to two goals from former Chelsea striker Liam Delap.

I'm not for jumping off the Nottingham Forest bandwagon just yet.

Forest have taken just four points from their last seven Premier League games - no team has taken fewer - yet they sit sixth in the expected points table for the season.

There is a significant disconnect between performance levels and results, something that usually corrects itself over time. I'm still a firm believer that Oliver Glasner will get this talented group of players motoring up the Premier League table.

And I'm struggling to see why Chelsea should command quite so much respect from the markets.

Of the ever-present Premier League teams in 2026, only one has lost more games than Chelsea (14) and only one has conceded more goals (51).

Where has Xabi Alonso's defensive magic gone?

His invincible Bayer Leverkusen side conceded just 24 league goals across their entire title-winning campaign in 2023/24. Chelsea have shipped 20 in 11 games this season alone. There is a softness to this Chelsea team when opponents turn up the intensity and attack them directly.

Just two clean sheets in their last 27 Premier League games tells a sorry tale.

Forest have the attacking weaponry to expose those defensive deficiencies.

The 29/20 with Sky Bet for a home win makes lots of sense.

Moises Caicedo has trained this week after coming off injured in the first half against Leeds United.

Chelsea will be without Joao Pedro, Maxence Lacroix, Jorrell Hato and Reece James .

Wesley Fofana , who this week apologised for conducting an unauthorised interview, will be available for selection.

Forest, meanwhile, will have midfielder Xaver Schlager and winger Callum Hudson-Odoi available.

They will be without midfielder Nicolas Dominguez and defender Nicolo Savona .

articles.title: El Madrid gana sin devorar kilómetros: líder de la Big 5 en eficiencia física
articles.standfirst: El equipo blanco encabeza un llamativo ranking de SkillCorner y CIES como el conjunto que menos distancia recorre por jugador en las cinco grandes ligas
articles.summary: El equipo blanco encabeza un llamativo ranking de SkillCorner y CIES como el conjunto que menos distancia recorre por jugador en las cinco grandes ligas
articles.body: Durante años se ha podido asumir que correr más era sinónimo de competir mejor. Que el esfuerzo físico, medido en kilómetros, era una condición indispensable para dominar en la élite. Sin embargo, el fútbol moderno empieza a demostrar que la eficiencia puede ser tan determinante como la intensidad. Y en ese apartado, nadie supera al Real Madrid. Según un estudio elaborado por SkillCorner y difundido por el CIES Football Observatory, el conjunto blanco es el equipo de las cinco grandes ligas europeas que menos distancia recorre por jugador y cada 90 minutos, con una media de 9,59 kilómetros. Un registro que sitúa al Madrid por delante de Getafe (9,67 km), Sevilla (9,78 km) y Manchester United (9,82 km), en una clasificación en la que también aparecen clubes como Liverpool, Chelsea, Betis o Everton. La cifra puede resultar sorprendente en un momento en el que el fútbol parece vivir una carrera constante hacia la hiperactividad física. Sin embargo, el dato no sugiere falta de intensidad. Más bien apunta a una gestión de esfuerzos especialmente eficaz. El Madrid no necesita recorrer tantos metros como sus rivales para imponer su superioridad. La calidad técnica de sus futbolistas, la capacidad para controlar los ritmos del partido y la enorme amenaza que genera en transición permiten al equipo resolver situaciones con menos desgaste. En otras palabras: corre menos porque muchas veces obliga a correr a los demás. Además, esta estadística tampoco mide la velocidad de los desplazamientos ni los esfuerzos explosivos. Un equipo puede recorrer menos kilómetros totales y, aun así, registrar más sprints, más aceleraciones o más acciones de alta intensidad. Precisamente ahí es donde suele marcar diferencias el conjunto madridista, capaz de decidir partidos con acciones vertiginosas de sus jugadores ofensivos. La clasificación también deja otra conclusión interesante. Entre los diez equipos que menos distancia recorren aparecen cinco representantes de LaLiga: Real Madrid, Getafe, Sevilla, Betis y Rayo Vallecano. Una presencia masiva que invita a pensar que el campeonato español continúa premiando más el control de los espacios, la organización táctica y la gestión de la posesión que el intercambio constante de golpes.

articles.title: Man Utd being relegated would be the biggest shock in history, but it won't happen, says Paul Merson
articles.summary: Manchester United take on Brentford on Saturday with Mauricio Pochettino looking for his first win to take them out of the relegation zone; Arsenal then take on Man City, live on Sky Sports this Sunday, the reigning champions are aiming to go nine points clear of Enzo Maresca's side
articles.body:
Mauricio Pochettino is looking for his first win as United boss as he bids to take them out of the relegation zone. However, Brentford visit Old Trafford on the back of their recent win over Everton, which took them into the top six.

Then on Sunday, Arsenal host title rivals Man City. Enzo Maresca's side are already six points behind the reigning champions and have won just two out of their last seven matches in all competitions.

Read below for the Magic Man's thoughts ahead of a huge weekend in the Premier League ...

Manchester United are in trouble. 100 per cent. Of course they are. But I don't see them getting relegated, absolutely not.

I would be shocked and amazed, it would be the biggest shock in the history of anything. People will go: Mike Tyson got beat by Buster Douglas. But that was one punch. This is over 38 games.

Brentford is a massive football match for them. If they lost that game, I don't see them beating Newcastle if Matthias Jaissle's side get anywhere near the level they played against Arsenal in the second half.

Then by the time you're playing Coventry, you're more than a win away from getting out of trouble. As soon as that starts happening, that's when it starts getting worrying - when you need two weeks to get out of the bottom three, or four or five points away.

The next three weeks are massive for United. If they beat Brentford this week, that will settle them down.

But I look at the teams down there right now. Crystal Palace won't go to Old Trafford and win. Sunderland and Nottingham Forest won't. Fulham and Coventry won't. Hull won't. So that means to me that Man Utd are better than them.

That's why I don't see them getting relegated. When you look at it like that, there are a lot of worse teams than them.

Man Utd have bought too many 'four or nines' - that's what I call them. They're either 4/10 or 9/10. They're not in between. You can't do that at Man Utd. You have to be between a seven or an eight on a consistent basis. You can't be four one week and nine the next, it doesn't work.

The pace of the game is controlled by the other team, it's never controlled by Manchester United.

They have got no defenders. They've gone it horribly wrong, trying to build from front to back. But it's more than that, it's spine of the team.

They need a centre forward. They don't have a dictating midfield player who comes short and controls the game. The only way United can do that is if they sacrifice Fernandes going forward and playing him deeper, like a quarterback - and then hope you've got enough going forwards elsewhere.

I don't see anyone else in that United team who is capable of coming deep and playing the ball forward. Playing that pass on a consistent basis, making the right decisions.

Man City have got to go out and play for the fans, they're the ones who are paying their money. They're getting paid £300,000-a-week, the fans are the ones paying to watch them.

Man City are getting a little bit found out. I have always said, even when they were playing at their best, they give you chances. And you have to make those chances count.

It used to be: go to the Etihad, get your stomach's tickled, get out with a 3-0 defeat that you're more than happy with that, and go back on the coach - because they could win games by six or seven.

Then all of a sudden, they started winning games but they were also open at the same time. And now, teams don't fear them.

Teams know they will get chances if they have a go at them - and enough chances to win football matches, not just one or two chances.

If you are brave enough - like Fulham were by getting players in the opposition box - you can beat Man City.

This is the problem for them: they're too open and there's not that fear factor anymore. And I also don't think Erling Haaland gets the service he deserves.

You would like to think that City's players aren't being affected by the charges hanging over them, because no one knows what is going to happen. So you have to play until you know what's going to happen.

It's like life: no one's going to tell you what's going to happen tomorrow, so live today.

'If Arsenal beat Man City, the league could be over soon'

If Arsenal win this game, the league is finished. That would be nine points clear and this league could be over very, very quickly.

Arsenal were dominant in the first half against Newcastle and if it was a boxing match, then Newcastle would have thrown the towel in.

They came out the second half a bit lackadaisical and Newcastle were outstanding by playing on the front foot. But then Arsenal switched and decided they weren't going to lose.

And then they scored one of the best goals of the season. If the finish from Noni Madueke was good, it would be the goal of the season. But when you see the finish, it's not great and the goalkeeper should save it. If he whips it into the far corner, it's goal of the season.

I think we saw enough with Brighton last weekend against Hull. That's one of those games where you go: if you can't win it, don't lose it.

You feel sorry for Brighton, because Konstantinos Tzolakis was unreal. He should be playing for the New York Rangers this weekend. He was like an ice hockey goalkeeper.

But if you're experienced team and you've been in that situation before, a draw is just a bad day at the office but we've played well, the goalkeeper's had a blinder and you don't lose a football match away from home. But they lost.

articles.title: Scottish Premiership: Can Rangers halt Falkirk to move top before Hearts host Celtic, live on Sky? Is time running out for Neil McCann at Kilmarnock?
articles.summary: Celtic are away to Hearts on Sunday, live on Sky Sports; Rangers host Falkirk; Aberdeen are at home to Dundee; St Mirren face Kilmarnock; Dundee United take on St Johnstone; Hibernian travel to Motherwell
articles.body:
Martin O'Neill's side are away to Hearts on Sunday, live on Sky Sports , meaning Rangers can move above them by ending Falkirk's six-game winning run - for 24 hours at least.

Kilmarnock risk being cast further adrift at the bottom, so is it win or bust for Neil McCann against St Mirren?

Here, we take a look at the big talking points ahead of this weekend's games...

Rangers are hoping to make it lucky 13 this weekend as they bid to reclaim top spot in the Scottish Premiership and put the pressure on Celtic.

They edged Aberdeen in a five-goal thriller in midweek to extend their unbeaten league run to 12 in the league. However, it was a performance Derek McInnes was not happy with, as he accused his players of "naivety" in the game.

The Ibrox side are on the longest unbeaten run in the league, but Falkirk are on the longest winning run as they continue to upset the odds to remain third in the table.

The Bairns were winless when Rangers beat them at the Falkirk Stadium earlier this season. Now, after winning six top-flight games in a row for the first time since 1966, they are looking to go one better.

Based on first halves only, no side would have more points in the Scottish Premiership this season than Falkirk (26, level with Celtic). Based on second halves, Rangers would be top (28 points).

A big week for Hearts and Celtic will end with a Premiership showdown at Tynecastle Park, live on Sky Sports.

The Jambos suffered a stoppage-time Conference League defeat to Monaco , while Celtic beat Torreense to secure back-to-back Europa League wins.

Martin O'Neill's side put seven past Wouter Vrancken's side earlier this season, but have failed to win on their last two visits to Gorgie.

Goals are not an issue for Hearts now. They became the first top-flight side to score eight goals in a single game since 2022, as they demolished Dundee at Dens Park last weekend.

The Jambos have scored in 21 successive league matches, the longest run by a non-Old Firm club for more than a decade.

The Hoops have won their last four games in all competitions. Will they make it five to guarantee they remain top, or will Hearts be able to get revenge?

Is time running out for McCann at Kilmarnock?

Kilmarnock are four points adrift at the bottom of the Premiership and have conceded a league-high 33 goals this season.

Neil McCann was not a popular appointment with the Killie fans, but he saved the side from relegation last season with the hope of better to come at Rugby Park.

If they lose at St Mirren on Saturday, they will have nine points after 15 games - just two of the last eight sides to have below 10 points at that stage of a top-flight campaign avoided relegation.

McCann and his players may take confidence from the fact that the Buddies are winless in their last four, and have scored fewer goals so far.

But one result would not ease the pressure completely, as the Killie fans demand another change less than a year after Stuart Kettlewell's departure.

While Neil McCann looks likely to be the next managerial casualty if results do not improve, there are other teams in need of a win.

St Mirren have won just four league games under Craig McLeish this season, while Motherwell have dropped to 11th after their late defeat to Rangers last time out.

Alfred Johansson believes his squad is finally getting to the position he wanted before the season started as players return from injury.

But, after a fourth-place finish under former boss Jens Berthel Askou, the Steelmen are in danger of being in this season's relegation battle. Defeat at home to Hibs on Saturday could leave them just one point ahead of Kilmarnock, if they manage to get a result.

Dundee made a strong start to the season, but have lost their last three games while conceding 12 goals.

Next is a trip to Aberdeen who appear rejuvenated under new head coach Mario Frick.

Steven Pressley said they got a "degree of pride back" against Hibs in midweek after being "embarrassed" by their 8-0 home defeat to Hearts.

Pride is one thing, but results are what matter.

articles.title: Pascal Gross and Luka Vuskovic helping drive Fabian Hurzeler's Brighton and their stunning Premier League start
articles.summary: There's a 16-year age gap between Gross, 35, and Vuskovic, 19, but the pair have been central to the stunning start Brighton have made to the Premier League; watch Brighton vs Newcastle live on Sky Sports Premier League on Sunday; kick-off 2.05pm
articles.body:
Yes, they were disappointed, but they weren't going to let a few minutes and Oli McBurnie overshadow a start to the season that has taken the Seagulls second in the Premier League table after 11 games.

Not many would have predicted such a lofty position for Fabian Hurzeler's team - including some of the Brighton team themselves - but the club are playing some thrilling football, and the 26 goals they have scored has helped them beat the likes of Arsenal and Man City already this season.

Sitting in front of me are two of the reasons why. They are both too modest to entertain that, but at the heart of this side's success is an almost seamless tactical and generational blend epitomised by Gross and Vuskovic.

Gross has been a revelation since his return earlier this year, something he admits he was nervous about doing. "You always hope for the best, but you never know. Coming back is not always easy."

The German international is making it look effortless. Opta have the 35-year-old top of their running stats, with 131.5km covered so far this league season, and only Declan Rice has more assists (4 vs 5).

But Gross' influence can't only be measured in numbers; this anchor or "connector" - as Hurzeler likes to call him - goes far beyond. No wonder his contract was recently extended for another season.

"I love the place, a lot of important things in my life happened here," he says.

"I have my family here, my kids are happy, my dog... it's a beautiful place with a lot of special people, where I feel really connected, really comfortable with the whole culture.

"We have so much talent and we have a lot of good people, but from different backgrounds. So that's really challenging, but I love the challenge because they're all good people we have in the dressing room.

"I was, at one point, a guy who came from another country, but I wanted to adapt, I wanted to be part of the culture. You need to help and support the guys. I really believe in what the club is doing. I think I can be a big part on and off the pitch."

The German international returned to Brighton after his dream move to Borussia Dortmund - the club he supported as a boy - ended early. He was desperate to show he could still perform at the highest level consistently. "I had to prove a point for myself, but also I wanted to repay the trust the club showed in me."

Do you remember playing better at any point in your career, I ask, telling him The Athletic had him as their number one player of the season so far.

"I don't believe in that. I don't see it like that. Maybe our start and the little things getting over-exaggerated.

"I think I am playing at my best, but maybe I think I'm a very good player in a good group who's working well, because everybody is improving. The way we set up, the way we play, I think everybody looks good."

Those stats, I say, are remarkable and again he down plays the praise. But he does concede: "They are really good, but because the team is playing well. If the team is playing well, everybody individually maybe looks a bit better."

Gross is honest enough to admit the start has surprised him. "No, I wouldn't say I expected that. I always hope for the best, but I know every game, like we saw on the weekend, is so different and so difficult that momentum can change quick."

Now, he says, comes the big challenge: the busy period. "It's a different sport, I always say". But you get the sense Brighton will be ready for it.

Alongside Gross, Vukovic has been another of the central characters in Brighton's success this season. He arrived in the summer from Tottenham in a club record deal worth £46m.

Vuskovic is no stranger to breaking records - two days after his 16th birthday, he became the youngest player to feature in Croatia's top flight. He is the fourth generation of his family to play football. Defending is very much the family business.

At 19, he has already played football in Croatia, Germany, Belgium and Poland, which has certainly helped him prepare for life as a central defender in the Premier League.

He says: "When you join as a 30-year-old guy, compared to say 15, instantly you have to grow up, you have to realise something in your life, and you have to mature.

"I had a really good group of people at Hajduk Split that made me mature fast enough, and they really helped me. In each of the countries, it was very helpful to develop, to grow as a human, as a football player."

Vuskovic's form in these first few months of the season has prompted a few questions about why Spurs let him leave in the summer and brought in Brighton's Paul van Hecke.

He doesn't see it as "rejection" and appreciates everything they did for him but, he adds: "In the end the coach came and said he didn't see me in his system, which is completely normal in football. I think in the end everybody earned (something). I gained experience, I moved to another club and I think we are all very happy about it.

"They told me they don't see me (as part of the plans), so there was no point in fighting for my place. I wanted to go somewhere where the coach would tell me, 'If you train well you will play', and that's exactly what happened here.

"The move, for me, was perfect. I love the players, I love the staff, the club. They've been all very nice to me since the first day I came, and I would change nothing."

For all the praise - and there has been plenty - Vuskovic is fiercely critical of himself. This is a player, after all, who employed a private analyst to make sure he was ready for the Premier League.

We talk about the two goals conceded late on against Hull he reflects: "I think I could have done more. We all could. We had our chances, but in the end, we didn't take them. Maybe we didn't have the luck. There's nothing to be sad or angry about, we can only learn from it and come back stronger."

If they keep learning and progressing what are this team capable of?

His reply? "Being at the top part of the Premier League, competing with all the top teams, also in Europe, if we are focused every game. Right now it's amazing, but we need to keep a clear head and just focus on what's next."

Pascal Gross and Luka Vuskovic were speaking at an American Express Shop Small campaign event aimed at encouraging people to support local businesses.

articles.title: Why Tottenham's Luca Williams-Barnett earned Lamine Yamal comparisons from Roberto De Zerbi
articles.summary: Sky Sports' Callum Bishop takes a look into Tottenham's next big hope Luca Williams-Barnett after the teenager signed a new long-term deal at the club; watch Sunderland vs Tottenham live on Sky Sports Main Event on Super Sunday; kick-off 2.05pm
articles.body:
So highly thought of is Luca Williams-Barnett at Tottenham that the remarks made following his stellar performance in the 2-0 win over Ipswich weren't all that shocking to hear.

"Luca is a special player. I'm not surprised because his talent is bigger than you think," De Zerbi said before simply saying, "yes, I think so," when asked if he could reach Lamine Yamal's level.

The 18-year-old wouldn't even be halfway through his second year of A-levels, but his talent hasn't been a secret. The likes of Bayern Munich and Manchester United had already been linked with the starlet, so the news of a long-term contract at Spurs is one that brings unbridled joy among the fanbase.

An England U19 international, Williams-Barnett made plenty of headlines in his first start. Most notably, he became Tottenham's third-youngest Premier League goalscorer at 18 years and 51 days, only four days older than Gareth Bale, who is second on the list. That name certainly rings a bell.

The winger was also Spurs' sixth-youngest Premier League starter, and it's not just with his club that he's making history.

Just three other players have scored on their first Premier League start at a younger age, while he is only bettered by future Ballon d'Or winner Michael Owen as the youngest player to score and grab an assist in the same game.

The records are a great indicator of the talent that the youngster has. Famous Spurs wonderkids such as Harry Kane, Dele Alli and Glenn Hoddle had yet to make an impact at that age.

But what is it about his game that is really making people stand up and take notice?

De Zerbi said after the Ipswich victory that he asked Williams-Barnett "to play like he plays at the park with his friends, with the same freedom".

It's the sort of cliché that you often hear levelled at emerging talents. Where they often lack in experience and nuance, they make up for in fearlessness and often youthful abandon.

De Zerbi's request was never going to be a challenge for the teenager, though. That trait is what had already earned him admirers from those in the know.

"He deserves the opportunity to play. He's got the swagger, he's got the ability to play in that team," was Tim Sherwood's assessment before he had even kicked a ball this season.

While the swagger can't be denied, his trademark on the pitch is rather straightforward. Williams-Barnett's tendency is to slow the play down and keep the ball close to his feet before showing explosive acceleration to catch his marker off guard.

Though it isn't necessarily the most groundbreaking piece of skill, the youngster possesses an abundance of composure that sees him capable of going on the inside or outside. Something that Anan Khalaili found out the hard way during the youngster's cameo against Crystal Palace.

It's the sort of foundational skill that gave the likes of Ronaldinho and Neymar a platform to develop into the greatest flair players of their generation. Funny that Williams-Barnett should bear some resemblance considering the Brazilian duo appear to play a role in his pre-match routine.

"I've seen today in the bus from the training ground to the stadium, because he was very close with me, while we were coming in the stadium, he was watching on YouTube Ronaldinho, [Eden] Hazard, Neymar," De Zerbi disclosed after the Ipswich win.

He is clearly taking inspiration from what he has seen from these idols. If we are being critical of those superstars, the one thing the youngster might want to avoid adopting from them is their desire off the ball, as his head coach has already challenged him to.

"Work hard without the ball, like [Ousmane] Dembele, like Raphinha, like [Lamine] Yamal, because football is going in a different way and the first defenders are the attackers. Even if they are Ballon d'Or winners, or any players with talent, they have to work on the pitch."

To that degree, the gauntlet has been set by De Zerbi. But there is no doubting that Williams-Barnett has the backing of those at Spurs to go and make himself a huge success.

"What stands out most for me is his courage and bravery because as a young lad coming into Spurs first team and performing like that is not easy. He will have a very big future," said team-mate Omar Marmoush.

It has been over a decade since the club had a youth product that has captured the imagination in quite this way. Kane is the most obvious example, but not even he immediately made fans pay attention to this extent.

As is the case with every young player, patience is a virtue. But with a new contract, De Zerbi's blessing and a start to Premier League life that could hardly go any better, the sky is the limit for Williams-Barnett.

It is far too early to say exactly how far he goes. But if he shoots for the moon and misses, he will still become one of the stars.

articles.title: Mourinho no habla con su 'primo' periodista: “Se ha cambiado a un grupo que me trata muy mal...”
articles.standfirst: El técnico portugués bromeó con su 'primo', Pedro Mourinho, periodista de CNN Portugal, al término de la rueda de prensa
articles.summary: El técnico portugués bromeó con su 'primo', Pedro Mourinho, periodista de CNN Portugal, al término de la rueda de prensa
articles.body: José Mourinho terminó la rueda de prensa con una presentación muy particular. Entre risas, señaló a uno de los periodistas presentes y desveló que era su 'primo', Pedro Mourinho, que trabaja en CNN Portugal. Pero la presentación vino acompañada de un recado sobre el trato que recibe en su país. Sin embargo, la realidad es que aunque comparten apellido... no tienen parentesco familiar alguno. “Este que está aquí es mi primo, que es uno de los mejores de los mejores periodistas de Portugal... pero se ha cambiado a un grupo que me trata muy, muy mal y yo no puedo hablar con él”, comentó entre risas. Una frase pronunciada en tono distendido, pero con bastante contexto detrás. Mourinho conoce bien la exigencia con la que se juzga su figura en Portugal. Su regreso al Benfica generó unas expectativas enormes. Muchos esperaban que su llegada cambiase de inmediato la dinámica del equipo y que obrase prácticamente un milagro. Sin embargo, los resultados y el rendimiento no estuvieron a la altura de todas esas expectativas y las críticas se hicieron especialmente duras. Los comentaristas portugueses llegaron a cuestionar abiertamente su capacidad y su vigencia como entrenador. “Está viejo, se le ha acabado la carrera, no entiende nada”, fueron algunos de los mensajes que tuvo que escuchar durante su última etapa en Portugal. Esa dureza contrasta con la consideración que todavía despierta Mourinho fuera de sus fronteras. Su figura sigue generando admiración y respeto en otros países, mientras que en Portugal la exigencia hacia uno de los entrenadores más reconocidos de su historia parece jugar en su contra. Por eso, la presentación de su primo acabó convirtiéndose en algo más que una anécdota familiar. Mourinho volvió a dejar un recado, esta vez entre sonrisas, sobre cómo siente que le tratan en su propio país.

articles.title: Man United vs Brentford: Premier League – Pochettino, predictions, lineups
articles.summary: Relegation-threatened Manchester United host Brentford in new manager Mauricio Pochettino’s first home game in charge.
articles.body:
Who : Manchester United vs Brentford What : Premier League, match day 12 Where : Old Trafford, Manchester, United Kingdom When : Saturday, November 28 at 3pm (15:00 GMT). How to follow : Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the build-up from 12:00 GMT before our live text commentary stream.

Manchester United’s newly-appointed manager Mauricio Pochettino takes charge of his first home game on Saturday, as his relegation-threatened team welcomes Brentford.

Pochettino has endured a rough start at Old Trafford, overseeing a 4-0 Premier League thrashing by rivals Liverpool on a disastrous debut, followed by a 2-2 draw with Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League.

Those results mean the Argentinian manager, who replaced the sacked Michael Carrick, is still searching for his first win as the United boss.

The Red Devils, once considered one of the best teams in the world, are languishing in the bottom three of the English top flight, having won only one league game all season, dating way back to August. Their points tally at this stage is their lowest in 54 years, highlighting the 13-time champions’ mighty fall.

London club Brentford, on the other hand, are in the top half of the standings, although Keith Andrews’s side are winless in their last five league away games and will be without main striker Igor Thiago once again due to suspension.

How have Manchester United played in the Premier League?

United are having one of their worst seasons in their history.

Pochettino’s side are second-bottom in the league standings with eight points from 11 games, having won only one game all season. Their points tally is the lowest at this stage since 1972-73.

The Red Devils have drawn five times and lost as many games, too.

United, who are yet to keep a clean sheet in this league campaign, are one point adrift of the safety zone.

How have Brentford played in the Premier League?

Brentford are playing far better than United, and sit sixth in the standings with 17 points after 11 games.

The Bees have won four matches, lost only twice and drawn five.

What happened the last time Manchester United and Brentford met?

When United and Brentford last met in the Premier League, it was United who earned a 2-1 home victory in that fixture on April 27.

An early goal from Casemiro coupled with another from Benjamin Sesko handed the hosts three points over Brentford, for whom Mathias Jensen was the lone scorer.

Predictions: Manchester United vs Brentford

Opta’s supercomputer has given United a slight edge over Brentford.

United have a 40.9 percent probability of victory on Saturday, while Brentford are predicted to have a 32.4 percent chance. There are 26.7 percent odds of a draw.

Bruno Fernandes is a doubt for the game after picking up a virus following the midweek trip to Portugal.

United already have a long list of injured players, including Marcus Rashford (hip) and Carlos Baleba (hamstring).

Winger Amad Diallo is doubtful with a knock, but left-back Luke Shaw is back in training after being out of action for more than a month.

Defender Leny Yoro, too, is available after the Football Association overturned his red card in the defeat at Anfield following a successful wrongful dismissal claim.

articles.title: Rodri está de vuelta y Lamine, O.K.
articles.standfirst: El centrocampista hizo parte del entrenamiento con sus compañeros; Bernal, no se ejercitó
articles.summary: El centrocampista hizo parte del entrenamiento con sus compañeros; Bernal, no se ejercitó
articles.body: Una de cal y otra de arena para Hansi Flick en el entrenamiento de este viernes. Por una parte, recupera a Rodri después de un mes sin poder contar con el centrocampista debido a una lesión. El futbolista se ha ejercitado este viernes con el resto de sus compañeros y todo hace indicar que entrará en la lista de convocados para jugar este domingo en Riazor frente al Deportivo. La idea es que pueda tener unos minutos frente al equipo gallego para ir adquiriendo ritmo y estar en óptimas condiciones de cara al importantísimo partido del próximo miércoles frente al Atlético de Madrid. Rodri se había lesionado en el bíceps femoral de la pierna derecha durante el encuentro frente al Aston Villa y ha estado casi cuatro semanas apartado de los entrenamientos. La otra buena noticia es Lamine Yamal. El extremo no viajó a Bakú por precaución por unas leves molestias en el tobillo. Tal y como se preveía ya está recuperado y podrá jugar el domingo. La cruz de la moneda la ha protagonizado Marc Bernal, que no se ha entrenado con el resto del grupo en la sesión de este viernes. El centrocampista tiene algunas molestias, aunque no son graves, y todo hace indicar que estará en condiciones de jugar en Riazor. Flick tendrá que decidir si lo incluye en la lista de convocados o si prefiere darle descanso para que llegue en plena forma al encuentro frente al Atlético. Christensen y Balde no estuvieron con el grupo y siguen recuperándose de sus lesiones. No es probable que entren en la convocatoria para La Coruña.

articles.title: Mendy vuelve a la vida... en un escenario complicado
articles.standfirst: Tras casi siete meses fuera, el francés regresa a una convocatoria con una dura competencia en el lateral izquierdo y el reto de dejar atrás un historial de lesiones
articles.summary: Tras casi siete meses fuera, el francés regresa a una convocatoria con una dura competencia en el lateral izquierdo y el reto de dejar atrás un historial de lesiones
articles.body: Ferland Mendy vuelve a la vida. Casi siete meses después de su último partido con el Real Madrid, el lateral francés vuelve a entrar en una convocatoria. Su regreso se ha hecho esperar más de lo previsto. Cuando pasó por el quirófano el pasado 11 de mayo, las estimaciones apuntaban a unos cinco meses de baja. Sin embargo, la complejidad de la lesión y sus antecedentes obligaron a extremar las precauciones y prolongaron una recuperación que ahora empieza a dar sus frutos. "La noticia buena es que Mendy mañana estará en el banquillo y eso es porque puede jugar. Un lesionado menos y uno más disponible. A pesar de que tenemos tres laterales izquierdos, que es demasiado, es una buena noticia que vuelva", anunció José Mourinho en rueda de prensa. Hay que remontarse al 3 de mayo para encontrar la última aparición del francés. Fue ante el Espanyol, en un partido que apenas pudo disputar unos minutos antes de sentir un fuerte dolor en el muslo derecho y abandonar el terreno de juego. Las pruebas confirmaron una lesión en el tendón del recto femoral, la misma zona que ya le había dado problemas anteriormente. Una semana después pasó por el quirófano para reparar la lesión. Los cinco meses de baja que se manejaron inicialmente terminaron convirtiéndose en casi siete. No era una lesión muscular más. Afectaba a una zona que ya había requerido una intervención quirúrgica en el pasado y que volvía a poner en duda su continuidad sobre el terreno de juego. El Real Madrid optó por la prudencia y evitó acelerar los plazos de un futbolista cuyo historial médico invitaba a no correr riesgos. Ahora, Mendy vuelve a estar disponible para Mourinho, aunque su regreso llega en un escenario complicado. El francés tendrá que competir por un puesto con Carreras y Cucurella, dos alternativas con las que cuenta el técnico para el lateral izquierdo. Además, su larga ausencia le obliga a recuperar sensaciones y demostrar que puede volver a encadenar partidos sin contratiempos. Su primera batalla ya la ha ganado, la de regresar después de una lesión que amenazaba con prolongar todavía más su ausencia. La siguiente será recuperar la continuidad que tantos problemas físicos le han impedido tener en las últimas temporadas Con las ausencias de Trent, Rodrygo, Asencio y Endrick, Mou tiene disponibles a casi la totalidad de sus efectivos.

articles.title: Brahim renueva hasta 2031 y se convierte en jugador 'intocable'
articles.standfirst: El malagueño terminaba contrato en 2027 y estaría así un lustro más de blanco
articles.summary: El futbolista malagueño terminaba contrato en 2026 y estaría así un lustro más de blanco
articles.body: ya es oficial: Brahim Díaz acaba de renovar por el Real Madrid. El conjunto blanco anunció hoy un acuerdo para renovarle el contrato a su delantero hasta 2031. El malagueño es considerado así por el club como pieza estructural en el futuro blanco, por mucho que José Mourinho ahora no le esté dando excesivos minutos. El internacional marroquí terminaba contrato en 2027, y se lo alarga hasta el próximo lustro (tiene 27 años). El chico ha rechazado ofertas súpermillonarias antes de firmar este nuevo contrato en el club donde quiere triunfar. Recordemos que la última vez que Brahim renovó con la entidad madridista fue en junio de 2023, siendo la finalización de su actual contrato en 2027, como hemos dicho. El internacional por Marruecos llegó a la entidad blanca en 2019 y su rendimiento, cuando les dan oportunidades, suele ser bueno. No está jugando ahora, pero queda mucha temporada y partidos por delante. El malagueño se prepara para un resto de temporada muy exigente a nivel colectivo y personal, con los tres compromisos de siempre (Liga, Copa y Champions), si bien la temporada tiene un último desafío allá por verano de 2027 con la Selección marroquí. En junio, en teoría , pues todo puede cambiar, habrá Copa África 2027 en Kenia, Uganda y Tanzania, con la fuerte presión de ganarla tras lo que pasó en la Copa 2025-26, con aquel penalti 'a lo Panenka', la final perdida en el campo y luego ganada en los despachos por la decisión de la CAF. El Real Madrid C. F. y Brahim Díaz han acordado la ampliación del contrato de nuestro jugador, que queda vinculado al club hasta el 30 de junio de 2031. Brahim llegó al Real Madrid en 2019 con 19 años. En sus seis temporadas defendiendo nuestra camiseta, ha disputado 173 partidos y ha ganado 7 títulos: 1 Champions League, 1 Mundial de Clubes, 1 Supercopa de Europa, 2 Ligas y 2 Supercopas de España. Es internacional con Marruecos, selección con la que ha jugado 36 partidos hasta el momento y ha marcado 15 goles. Fue el máximo goleador de la Copa África 2025.

articles.title: ESPN College GameDay 2026 Week 13 Location Hosts, TV Schedule and Predictions
articles.summary: ESPN's College GameDay has largely been centered around SEC and Big Ten matchups this season. For Week 13, though, the premier pregame show will head to Winston-Salem, North Carolina to preview a massive ACC showdown.
articles.body:
ESPN's College GameDay has largely been centered around SEC and Big Ten matchups this season. For Week 13, though, the premier pregame show will head to Winston-Salem, North Carolina to preview a massive ACC showdown.

The crew will be on site at Hearn Plaza ahead of Wake Forest's finale against Duke.

Week 13 will bring plenty of rivalry games to the forefront, but this one will have huge implications, both in the conference race and in the College Football Playoff (CFP) picture.

Venue: Hearn Plaza (in front of Wait Chapel) on Wake Forest's campus in Winston-Salem, North Carolina

Crew: Rece Davis, Kirk Herbstreit, Desmond Howard, Pat McAfee, and Nick Saban

Wake Forest has become one of this year's darlings and can come another step closer to the CFP with a win this week. The Demon Deacons have only lost once this season, a 33-20 loss to seventh-ranked Miami.

Miami and Wake Forest are already set to meet again in the ACC title game on December 5. However, reaching that game with a one-loss record could be huge for the Demon Deacons.

The winner of the conference title game will earn an automatic berth into the playoff. However, the loser could still sneak into the 12-team field with a close loss, provided it holds a top-12 spot entering the game. A loss to the 7-4 Blue Devils could drop Wake Forest out of the top 12.

Miami, meanwhile, must survive Boston College this weekend.

Wake Forest has been dominant as of late and is unsurprisingly viewed as a heavy favorite. Gio Lopez and the Demon Deacons' offense have been carving up opposing defenses to the tune of 44.5 points per game. Langston Hardy and the Wake Forest defense have surrendered just 16.3 points per game.

However, this doesn't mean that the Demon Deacons shouldn't be on upset alert. According to head coach Jake Dickert, they won't take the opposition lightly.

"I'm not worried about the ACC championship game," Dickert said, per Aaron Beard of the Associated Press. "We're in a Big Four rivalry week, a team we haven't beaten in four years, played all kind of close games. … They've got our full attention."

Duke won last year's matchup 49-32, has won four straight meetings in the rivalry series, and has fielded a pretty solid squad this season. Manny Diaz's team has averaged 30.2 points while allowing just 15.7 points per game.

If the defense can shut down Lopez and Co., while star running back Nate Sheppard wears down Wake Forest's defense, the Blue Devils will have a shot to win outright. The prediction here is that they at least keep it uncomfortably close.

articles.title: Women's Super League: Ipswich Women sign Princess Ademiluyi for record fee
articles.summary: Ipswich Town Women confirm the permanent signing of England youth international Princess Ademiluyi for a club record fee.
articles.body:
Ipswich Town Women have confirmed the permanent signing of England youth international Princess Ademiluyi for an undisclosed club record fee.

The 20-year-old forward has been on loan at the Tractor Girls from NWSL side Gotham FC since February and has agreed a three-and-a-half year deal at the WSL2 side.

Ademiluyi has been capped by England at under-19 and under-20 level, and has been called up for the under-23 side for the first time ahead of their internationals against Belgium and Portugal next week. , external

"I have really made a home for myself in Suffolk and I am so excited to continue building what has been a positive start to the season for us as a group," she told the club's website. , external

"The players, staff and supporters have all been brilliant with me since I arrived and I can't wait to see where this club can go and to continue making more memories together."

Ipswich Town chairman Mark Ashton said: "Signing Princess on a permanent basis has been a real priority for us and completing such a significant deal as this highlights the club's ongoing commitment to reach the top level of the game.

"This is a statement signing for the club, with further announcements to come in due course as we reaffirm our commitment to our women's set-up in both the short and long-term."

Ademiluyi started her career at WSL side West Ham in 2023 before moving to US-based Gotham and is Ipswich's top scorer so far in 2026-27, with four goals.

The Tractor Girls finished ninth in WSL2 last season following promotion to the second tier in 2025, and were in the fourth tier as recently as 2021. , external

Under the management of former men's team player David Wright, appointed to the role in April, the Blues are third after eight games this season, three points behind leaders Newcastle United.

Ipswich on 'inevitable' path to WSL - Boswell

Ademiluyi has played an important role in helping the Tractor Girls transform from relegation candidates to title contenders.

She made an immediate impact on joining in February, scoring goals against Durham and Birmingham City to help secure the team's survival in WSL2.

The forward has continued to find the net this season, and won the WSL2 player of the month award for October. , external

There is a growing feeling within the women's game that the Blues will be playing at the highest level in the not too distant future and securing a proven goalscorer whose stock is also rising on the international stage will only strengthen that train of thought.

articles.title: European football violence causes concern with far-right claim in UEFA game
articles.summary: Claims of Nazi salutes at UEFA Europa League game in Marseille headline night of further violence in European football.
articles.body:
Violent clashes at two European football matches have stoked concerns about fan violence and prompted the leaders of France and Bulgaria to condemn behaviour that had “no place in civilized Europe”.

Images showed masked ⁠and bloodied fans wielding improvised weapons and metal pipes during a brawl at a UEFA Europa League match on Wednesday evening between Marseille and Levski Sofia, which the Bulgarian club said began when their fans were attacked by supporters of the French side.

A photographer working for the Reuters news agency ⁠said the clashes at the Stade Velodrome in Marseille had started after a supporter from the visitors’ stand made a Nazi salute.

Clashes also broke out at a Europa League match in the Georgian city of Batumi between Turkiye’s Besiktas and Israel’s Hapoel Be’er Sheva, forcing the referee to suspend the match for 30 minutes.

European football’s governing body UEFA told Reuters its disciplinary body “would assess the match reports before considering any potential ‌next steps”.

What was the reaction to the Marseille and Levski Sofia game?

Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev said he and French President Emmanuel Macron spoke by phone and condemned the violence at the Marseille-Levski Sofia match, in which Marseille police said 11 Bulgarian fans were hurt, five of whom were taken to hospital.

“We share the position that aggression and violence have no place in civilized Europe,” Radev said on Facebook.

“I thank President Macron for his personal commitment to this case, for the medical care provided to the injured by the French authorities, for the measures taken to ensure the safety of Bulgarian citizens, and for the perpetrators to be held accountable.”

Macron said he had condemned “with the utmost ⁠force” acts of violence targeting Bulgarian fans, which he said had “no place in sport or in ⁠public space”, and told Radev they would not go unpunished.

A protest was planned in front of the French embassy in Sofia ⁠later on Friday.

French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said: “Violence, racial hatred and provocation have no place in our stadiums.”

Manuel Bompard, a French lawmaker for the hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) party in the Marseille department, commented on a video on social media appearing to show a Levski fan performing a Nazi salute.

“Congrats to the Marseille fans who responded with an antifascist chant,” Bompard wrote on X. “The far-right has no place in our stadiums!”

Batons fly, flares lit in Marseille and Levski Sofia clash

Levski Sofia, which lost the match 1-0, said masked fans had attacked its supporters with batons and flares. Some had let off flares and tried to get through ⁠the barrier as security staff tried to hold them back.

Images showed fans attacking each other through a netted fence separating sections of the stadium.

Before Thursday’s match, French authorities had introduced a sevenfold reduction of ticket sales to Levski supporters and imposed additional restrictions on their movement to and ⁠around the stadium, aiming to curb risks of violence.

The Bulgarian Ministry of Foreign Affairs said it would request a ⁠thorough investigation. Marseille said it would conduct its own analysis and was working closely ⁠with law enforcement.

What happened in the Besiktas and Hapoel Be’er Sheva match?

The match between Besiktas and Hapoel Be’er Sheva had been moved from Istanbul for what UEFA said were safety and security reasons.

Clashes in the stands led referee Morten Krogh to suspend the match in the 26th minute, and it resumed after a 30-minute delay. Georgian police entered the stands, and television footage showed one ‌fan being carried out on a stretcher.

Turkish outlet NTV reported that police used pepper spray. Besiktas condemned what it called “disproportionate force” by security staff and said a number of fans had been denied entry. Besiktas went on to win 2-1.

Turkish Football Federation chair Ibrahim Haciosmanoglu defended the ‌decision ‌to keep Israeli clubs out of Turkiye following Israel’s invasion of Gaza in 2023 after the deadly Hamas-led attacks on southern Israel.

articles.title: Watch video: Police storm training pitch in Brazil to arrest top-flight footballer David Correa mid-session over serious criminal allegations
articles.summary: In a shocking turn of events, David Correa, a 31-year-old forward for Vasco da Gama, was arrested by Brazilian police during a training session amid serious allegations including attempted homicide and drug trafficking.
articles.body: Bizarre scenes unfolded at a Brazilian top-flight football club on Thursday morning as police officers arrived at Vasco da Gama's training ground and arrested one of their first-team players in the middle of a training session. The player, 31-year-old forward David Correa, is being investigated over alleged involvement in attempted homicide, drug trafficking and organised crime, leaving the club facing uncertainty over his immediate playing future and contractual situation.David Correa arrested during Vasco da Gama trainingPolice officers arrived at the training ground of Vasco da Gama, formally known as Club de Regatas Vasco da Gama, a Rio de Janeiro-based club competing in the Campeonato Brasileiro Série A (Brasileirão), Brazil's top division, on Thursday morning and arrested Correa while he was participating in a first-team training session. Dressed in the club's training kit, the 31-year-old was on the pitch when officers detained him. They were executing a pretrial detention warrant connected to an investigation led by the Espírito Santo Civil Police, with agents from the 14th Police Precinct in Leblon carrying out the arrest.According to Brazilian outlet ge, Correa was still on the training pitch when officers entered the facility. He was taken to the 14th Police Precinct to give a statement before being transferred to the José Frederico Marques prison in Benfica, in the north of Rio de Janeiro, where he arrived on Thursday evening.The 31-year-old is being investigated over alleged involvement in attempted homicide, drug trafficking and membership of an armed criminal organisation. Authorities are also examining suspected links between Correa and members of the Comando Vermelho criminal faction, as well as allegations of weapons trafficking, money laundering, witness intimidation and attempts to interfere with judicial proceedings.Correa has previously denied involvement in drug or arms trafficking. His arrest follows an earlier court order, issued in late October, requiring him to surrender his passport. The investigation subsequently intensified, with reports suggesting that authorities were examining possible attempts to bribe witnesses and influence their accounts.The case also involves another professional footballer, Hayner William Monjardim Cordeiro, then associated with second-division club Vila Nova and on loan from Santos. Both players were investigated as part of a wider police operation examining suspected connections between professional footballers and organised criminal networks.An earlier phase of the investigation involved searches at Correa's home in the Barra da Tijuca district of Rio de Janeiro and at Vasco's training ground. According to the Associated Press, the operation, known as The Troop, involved approximately 100 officers and resulted in four arrest warrants and 15 search warrants being executed. Correa reportedly left the training facility at the time without answering questions from journalists.The allegations and the investigation into organised crimeThe investigation centres on alleged connections to drug and weapons trafficking, money laundering and criminal activity in Espírito Santo. Correa is also being investigated over alleged involvement in an attempted homicide, while authorities are examining whether he had links to members of Comando Vermelho.The latest escalation has brought particular attention to allegations of witness intimidation and attempts to interfere with the judicial process. Reports cited by ABC Deportes indicate that investigators are examining the possibility that witnesses were offered money to change their accounts, adding another dimension to the case.Correa has not been convicted of any crime, and the allegations remain subject to the ongoing judicial process. His previous denial of involvement in drug and arms trafficking is also relevant as the investigation continues.The arrest has nevertheless created an immediate problem for Vasco, who must now consider how to handle a first-team player facing serious criminal allegations while respecting the legal process.What Correa's arrest means for his Vasco contractVasco da Gama are examining their legal options following Correa's detention, including whether they can suspend his employment contract and associated financial obligations while he remains unable to play.Brazilian labour legislation, particularly the Consolidation of Labour Laws (CLT), provides a framework for employment-related decisions when an employee cannot fulfil their duties. The General Sports Law also contains a specific provision for professional athletes whose absence is unrelated to their sporting activity.Under Article 88 of the General Sports Law, a club may suspend an athlete's special sports employment contract if the player is unable to perform his duties for more than 90 consecutive days because of circumstances that are exclusively his own responsibility and unrelated to his sporting activity.For Vasco to use that provision, the club would need to issue formal notice and register the suspension with the Brazilian Football Confederation's National Registration System. A suspension could affect salary payments, contributions to the employee severance fund, known as FGTS, and other employment benefits.Terminating the contract outright is more complicated. Under the legal framework described in the reporting, dismissal for cause on the basis of a criminal case requires a final conviction with no further avenue of appeal. Correa remains under investigation and has not been convicted, meaning Vasco cannot simply treat the allegations as proof of wrongdoing.If the club decides to part ways with him before that point, it would need to consider a negotiated mutual termination or the compensation obligations attached to ending his sporting contract.Correa had already missed Vasco's recent fixture against Bragantino before his arrest, and his availability is now uncertain as the proceedings in Espírito Santo continue. His defence can also challenge the preventive detention through a habeas corpus petition.A regular in Vasco's squad since 2024Correa has been part of Vasco's setup since 2024 and has become a regular member of the Rio de Janeiro club's squad. He has made 117 appearances across competitions, scoring 15 goals and providing 10 assists. During the 2026 season, he has featured in 46 matches and scored six goals.He also started Vasco's second-leg Copa Sudamericana semi-final against Boca Juniors at the Maracanã, although he was substituted at half-time. The fixture attracted attention in Argentina, where his involvement in the match had been reported in the weeks before his arrest.Vasco da Gama are scheduled to return to action on Monday, November 30, 2026, when they travel to face Clube Atlético Mineiro in an away fixture in the Campeonato Brasileiro Série A. Correa's availability for the match remains uncertain following his arrest and ongoing legal proceedings.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Raúl García desvela cómo eran sus duelos con Sergio Ramos: "Yo era un poco menos caliente que Sergio"
articles.standfirst: El exfutbolista repasa en La Pizarra de Quintana su trayectoria, su frustrado fichaje por el Valencia y los motivos de su retirada
articles.summary: El exfutbolista repasa en La Pizarra de Quintana su trayectoria, su frustrado fichaje por el Valencia y los motivos de su retirada
articles.body: Raúl García, tercer futbolista con más partidos en la historia de LaLiga, ha pasado por los micrófonos de La Pizarra de Quintana, en Radio MARCA, para someterse al particular 'test de cotillitas' de Miguel Quintana, Adrián Blanco y Álex de Llano. El exjugador de Osasuna, Atlético de Madrid y Athletic Club ha repasado las mejores anécdotas de su carrera, sus enfrentamientos con Sergio Ramos y su relación con los entrenadores que marcaron su trayectoria. Con 609 partidos en Primera División, el navarro se mostró orgulloso del camino recorrido por encima de cualquier registro estadístico. "Para mí, más que el número en sí, lo que significa es el trabajo que hay detrás", explicó. Pese a quedarse a sólo 13 encuentros de Joaquín y Zubizarreta, nunca se planteó prolongar su carrera para superarles: "No voy a jugar un año más por el hecho de superar un récord. No me va a cambiar mi carrera". Preguntado por el rival más complicado al que se ha enfrentado, Raúl García no dudó en mencionar a Sergio Ramos. Pese a los numerosos encontronazos que protagonizaron sobre el terreno de juego, el navarro desveló la buena relación que mantienen fuera de él. "Nosotros cuando competimos competimos desde esa nobleza de ir con todo, pero yo con Sergio tengo muy buena relación". El exfutbolista también explicó cómo gestionaba aquellos enfrentamientos: "Yo era un poco menos caliente que Sergio, fíjate lo que te digo. Yo me manejaba un poquito mejor, diría". Incluso reconoció que había espacio para las bromas en mitad de los duelos: "En el momento que estás chocando, que estás peleando y tal, haces bromas". Raúl García recordó que estuvo muy cerca de vestir la camiseta del Valencia antes de incorporarse al Atlético de Madrid. "En 2007 yo con Valencia tuve conversaciones bastante avanzadas", desveló. Finalmente, su destino fue el conjunto rojiblanco, una decisión de la que no se arrepiente. El navarro también reconoció su admiración por la Premier League y, especialmente, por el Liverpool. "Es una Liga que me gusta y que la sigo", explicó, antes de confesar su predilección por el conjunto de Anfield: "Por lo que sea, le tengo algo. Es algo que me parece atractivo". Entre todos los entrenadores que marcaron su carrera, Raúl García destacó especialmente a Javier Aguirre, el técnico que le hizo debutar y que también influyó en su llegada al Atlético de Madrid. "Javier Aguirre ha sido y es una persona fundamental no en mi carrera, sino también en mi vida", aseguró. El exrojiblanco recordó también la incertidumbre que vivió antes de regresar al Atlético tras su segunda etapa en Osasuna, coincidiendo con la llegada de Diego Pablo Simeone al banquillo: "Ellos sí tenían claro que me iba a quedar, yo no", explicó sobre las conversaciones que mantenía con sus excompañeros. Ni siquiera la final de Champions perdida con el Atlético le hace querer cambiar algún episodio de su trayectoria. "Esa pregunta me la han hecho muchas veces y no cambiaría nada. Las cosas van como tienen que ir", afirmó. "Yo he aprendido mucho más cuando ha ido mal que cuando ha ido bien". Alejado ya de la exigencia del fútbol profesional y con el pádel como una de sus grandes aficiones, Raúl García reconoció que disfruta de la tranquilidad y del tiempo que ahora puede dedicar a su familia. Tanto es así que dejó una sorprendente reflexión sobre su retirada: "Si yo iba a tener esta sensación antes, igual me hubiese retirado un par de años antes para poder disfrutar". El navarro también puso en valor la importancia del trabajo psicológico en el deporte de élite, recordando cómo la falta de confianza puede condicionar el rendimiento de un futbolista: "Cuando las cosas no te salen, cuando tienes dudas, cuando dudas de si eres capaz o no, de repente parece que te has olvidado de jugar al fútbol".

articles.title: Why did Georgian police clash with Turkish football fans over Palestine?
articles.summary: Georgia’s Interior Ministry says 16 people were detained and three employees injured during clashes.
articles.body:
Police in Georgia have detained at least 16 people following clashes between football fans at a game between Turkish and Israeli clubs.

The Europa League fifth round match between Turkiye’s Besiktas and Israel’s Hapoel Be’er Sheva was hosted in Georgia instead of Turkiye.

The coastal Georgian city of Batumi was selected last month as a neutral territory to host the game for “safety and security reasons” because of fears of protests over Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, according to the European football association, UEFA.

Despite the precaution, tensions between fans spilled over into the stadium and the match was suspended for 30 minutes. Once play resumed, Besiktas won the game 2-1.

It is not the first time violent clashes have marred football matches involving Israeli clubs since Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza began in October 2023.

Here’s what we know about the latest unrest:

What happened in Besiktas and Hapoel Be’er Sheva’s game?

Tensions between fans had already been rising before kickoff in Batumi on Thursday.

According to the Georgian news outlet Civil Georgia, videos on social media showed groups of Besiktas fans marching through Batumi and physical confrontations between fans and police officers.

Turkiye’s Anadolu Agency reported that the Besiktas players refused to shake hands with their Hapoel opposition.

In the 26th minute, the game was temporarily suspended when clashes broke out between Georgian police and Besiktas supporters. Turkish media outlets reported that police entered the stands and used pepper spray against Turkish fans.

According to reports, the police involvement came after a fan displayed a Palestinian flag and banner.

Turkiye’s TRT World reported that police surrounded the fan and used pepper spray, adding that video later showed a Besiktas fan being carried out on a stretcher and others being injured during the intervention.

What have Turkiye and Georgia said after Europa League match?

Omer Celik, spokesperson and deputy chairman of Turkiye’s ruling AK party, posted on X that the “intervention and violence” against the Besiktas fans who unfurled a ‘FREEDOM FOR PALESTINE’ banner and held a Palestine flag was “unacceptable”.

“Besiktas fans spoke on behalf of the alliance of humanity and became the voice of humanity. We strongly condemn the Israeli team’s provocations on the pitch. We extend our best wishes for a speedy recovery to our fans who were injured in the incidents and taken to hospital. We are closely monitoring the condition of our citizens,” Celik said.

But Georgian Interior Minister Sulkhan Tamazashvili told reporters that UEFA officials confiscated the fans’ Palestine flags and Georgian state authorities played no role in the confiscation.

Tamazashvili said that 16 people were detained and three ministry employees injured.

“While marching from European Square towards Batumi Arena, some of the fans of the football club ‘Besiktas’ stood out by their aggressive actions,” the ministry said in a statement.

“They violated the public order by making indecent shouting and shooting of various objects, disobeyed the legal demands of the police, resisted law enforcement and physically confronted them.”

Police took appropriate measures to curb the violence, de-escalate incidents and ensure public safety, including the use of what it called “special means”, the ministry added.

It denied that the use of force was related to the display of pro-Palestine banners and flags.

“We categorically deny this information and emphasise that violent actions by fans and physical confrontation with law enforcers prior to the display of flags and banners have just begun while marching towards the stadium.”

How have Besiktas and other Turkish clubs responded?

Besiktas said it condemned the use of “disproportionate force”.

“We have initiated formal inquiries with our Consulate General in Batumi and with UEFA regarding the disproportionate force used by security personnel against our supporters; we will continue to monitor the situation closely until every single one of our supporters has returned home safely,” read a club statement.

In a post on X congratulating the Besiktas victory, the Turkish Football Federation said it would “closely monitor the unacceptable behaviour directed at our club, Besiktas and our supporters in Batumi tonight, and that we will take action with the relevant authorities to ensure that these incidents are fully investigated and the necessary steps are taken.”

Other Turkish Super Lig clubs, including Trabzonspor, Fenerbahce, Galatasaray, Erzurumspor, Basaksehir and Samsunspor, also condemned the use of force against Besiktas fans.

Why was Georgia hosting a UEFA match between Israeli and Turkish teams?

Since the onset of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza three years ago, Turkish clubs have not hosted Israeli opposition at home because of security concerns, with matches played in neutral territories instead.

Turkish-Israeli relations have taken a downturn since the war began, with Turkish authorities taking a hard line against the military policies of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government in the occupied Palestinian territories.

However, Georgia and Israel have good relations with close ties maintained amid the war.

Israel’s far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir was in the capital Tbilisi for a diplomatic visit last year.

What’s Europe’s track record when dealing with pro-Palestine fans?

Last year, English club Aston Villa hosted a Europa League game against Maccabi Tel Aviv , but security concerns prompted West Midlands Police to recommend the banning of Israeli fans from the game.

The decision was taken following violence after a match in Amsterdam between Maccabi and Dutch side Ajax. Police intervened against protesters and Israeli media framed the clashes as a “violent, anti-Semitic pogrom”.

In 2024, another match between Ajax and Maccabi Tel Aviv led to clashes between fans of the Israeli team and pro-Palestine protesters, as Maccabi fans burned Palestinian flags and attacked homes displaying them.

articles.title: Arbeloa vuelve a pescar en el Madrid
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Fulham incorpora a Jesús Rueda como segundo entrenador y continúa rodeándose de profesionales y jóvenes talentos con pasado blanco
articles.summary: El técnico del Fulham incorpora a Jesús Rueda como segundo entrenador y continúa rodeándose de profesionales y jóvenes talentos con pasado blanco
articles.body: Álvaro Arbeloa sigue construyendo su proyecto en el Fulham con una clara mirada hacia el Real Madrid. El técnico español no ha olvidado su etapa en Valdebebas y continúa recurriendo a personas con las que compartió vestuario y trabajo en la cantera y el primer equipo blanco. El último en incorporarse a su aventura en la Premier League ha sido Jesús Rueda, que llega a Craven Cottage para ejercer como segundo entrenador. La conexión entre ambos viene de su etapa en el Real Madrid, donde coincidieron durante la temporada 2025/26. Rueda formó parte inicialmente del cuerpo técnico de Xabi Alonso como especialista en acciones a balón parado y, tras la llegada de Arbeloa al banquillo en enero, pasó a desempeñar funciones de análisis táctico y apoyo al equipo. Su salida del club blanco en verano puso fin a aquella etapa, aunque no a su relación profesional con el técnico salmantino. De hecho, la sintonía entre ambos quedó patente en la despedida pública de Rueda del Real Madrid. El analista definió su experiencia en el primer equipo como "cumplir un sueño que llevaba conmigo desde niño" y agradeció expresamente la confianza de Xabi Alonso y Arbeloa. El actual entrenador del Fulham tampoco quiso dejar pasar la ocasión para dedicarle unas palabras en los comentarios de la publicación: "¡Ha sido un lujo poder trabajar a tu lado!". Un mensaje que cobra ahora especial significado tras volver a unir sus caminos en Inglaterra. Pero Jesús Rueda no es el único nombre vinculado al Real Madrid que ha encontrado acomodo en el proyecto londinense. Arbeloa también ha recurrido al talento de La Fábrica para reforzar su plantilla con Gonzalo García, César Palacios y Manuel Ángel. Tres futbolistas que conocen bien su metodología y con los que mantiene una relación de confianza desde su etapa en Valdebebas. Así, el técnico continúa trasladando parte de su universo madridista a la Premier League, tanto en el banquillo como sobre el terreno de juego.
