articles.title: Ryan Naderi: Rangers manager Derek McInnes hopes to tie down striker as Jamestown Analytics search revealed
articles.summary: Rangers signed Ryan Naderi from German third-division side Hansa Rostock in a £4.7m deal in the winter window; the striker's current deal runs until 2029 but Sky Sports News revealed he wants to extend that stay; he has 11 goals and seven assists in 19 games across all competitions
articles.body:
But the Rangers boss is now encouraging Ibrox chief executive Jim Gillespie to do what he can to tie down the Czechia international for the longer term.

When Hearts manager, McInnes asked sporting director Graeme Jones to check how the striker was rated by data partner Jamestown Analytics as Rangers negotiated with German third-division outfit Hansa Rostock.

McInnes said: "You're always curious. It's brilliant when you see other teams round about you signing a player that's not rated, it's just natural.

"But he was someone that was well known to them [Jamestown Analytics]. I think Club Brugge had an interest in Ryan and Union Saint-Gilloise potentially had an interest in him as well. But the fee just went away from them.

"We were told that he was a good player before I'd even set eyes on him, and the feeling was that he could help Rangers and make them better.

"So when I'd seen a lot of the comings and goings, it was on, it was off, it was on again, I was kind of hoping that it would fall through, being the Hearts manager."

Naderi scored his first Scottish Premiership goal in early April to help Rangers go top of the table for the first time in more than two years, but he soon went off with an injury and watched from the sidelines as Danny Rohl's team blew their title hopes.

The German-born forward has proven a key player under McInnes, taking his season tally to 11 goals and seven assists in 19 games across all competitions this season, and Rangers are looking at Naderi's long-term future.

Sky Sports News revealed on Wednesday that the player was keen to extend his Ibrox contract, which currently runs until 2029.

"These conversations I have with Jim on a regular basis about players that we should be speaking to and give them a wee bit more security and a wee bit more comfort for us," McInnes said.

"So these conversations have been ongoing. The club's well aware of what needs to be done and what we shouldn't be doing. And Ryan's been part of that conversation."

Boyd: Where would Rangers be without Naderi?

"Aside from the game against Dundee, he's had a goal or an assist in every single game since coming on here against Motherwell [in September], when he had been out of the team.

"There's been a lot of players who've had plaudits, but where would Rangers be without Naderi?

"When a lot of games have been tied, it always seems to be [that he scores] the first goal, or the goal that puts Rangers ahead, or the goal that seals it.

"He's scored key goals. Go back to the [League Cup] semi-final, he found a way there. He found a way at Celtic Park to get the ball in the net as well.

"Him and Kelsy didn't really work against Aberdeen, but you can understand why Derek left Naderi on the pitch, because he's the one that's assisting, he's the one that's scoring goals, he's always in and around."

articles.title: Bruno Fernandes: Man Utd activate captain's 12-month option to extend contract which now ends in 2028
articles.summary: Bruno Fernandes' contract was expiring at the end of this season but it will now run until the summer of 2028; the Man Utd captain and the club are in agreement that it makes sense to return to negotiations in the future, with full focus on improving the club's current position
articles.body:
His deal was previously set to expire at the end of this season but will now run until summer 2028.

United have been in talks with Fernandes over extending his contract since the summer.

Sky Sports News understands both parties are in agreement that it makes sense to return to negotiations in the future - with full focus on improving the club's current position.

Triggering the club option now is logical from United's perspective, as clubs could have approached Fernandes over a pre-contract agreement in January. This contract clause activation prevents that.

Meanwhile, Fernandes was absent from United training on Friday - ahead of their game against Brentford on Saturday - due to illness.

Fernandes is understood to be under the weather and is being kept away from the squad ahead of the Brentford game.

On whether he'll make the game, Mauricio Pochettino said: "We don't know. He got a virus in Portugal. He finished the game with a problem and today he cannot be part of the training session.

"We'll see. We are going to see during the day, and [Saturday], how he wakes up. We are not going to take any risks."

Fernandes extension protects Man Utd from losing captain on a free

"What triggering this option does is reduce the chance to zero that any club outside of the Premier League can approach Fernandes from Europe's top leagues around a potential move next summer for free.

"So this move protects both the club and the player from that situation.

"We know he's been the subject of interest in the last few summers, especially from Saudi Arabia.

"I think negotiations will continue in the future over Fernandes' long-term future, but for now he will remain at the club until the summer of 2028."

'Man Utd can't fall out with their best player'

"They are protecting their asset. It is as simple as that. They are not in a position to fall out with their best player.

"They need him to go and perform to make sure they do not go down. I do not think they are in a relegation fight; they have the manager who will sort a lot of things out.

"Right now, they are a team devoid of all confidence. They could lose to Brentford, but I do not think they are in a relegation fight. They will end up finishing in mid-table.

"They have some very average players, hence the position, but they needed to trigger the clause to protect the asset and then get the money in the summer, if they have to."

What Fernandes and Man Utd have said on contract talks

Last week, Fernandes exclusively told Sky Sports that United have offered him a new contract - but he has put discussions on hold as he insists the club's priority must be returning to winning ways.

Fernandes has rejected two contract offers from United . The club's initial proposal was made in the summer when discussions first began over a new deal, but was turned down by the Portuguese, who signed his last contract in August 2024.

The United captain said: "I've seen people saying that he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years. If I wanted more money, I wouldn't be here.

"I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester.

"Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here. The thing is, I've always showed how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club. And I always said, in the moment the club thinks it's time for me to move on, I will move on.

"I'm not going to be the player that I've seen many in this time at Manchester United. They're going to stay here just by staying, just finish my contract and then we will see. In the moment the club says, 'Bruno, it's time to part ways', I'm going to be the first one walking out the door.

"Yeah, the club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay. And there are no negotiations going on. We spoke about the contract at the end of last season, we came in the beginning of this season speaking about the contract.

"But about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to one side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations because the most important thing now is that the club gets back to win games.

"My aim will always be to win the Premier League and the Champions League within the club I am."

Man Utd chief executive Omar Berrada also spoke to Sky Sports last week about Fernandes' contract talks and said: "Listen, I've said before, we have a tremendous amount of respect for Bruno. We're very fortunate to have him as a captain.

"What he's done for this team over the last six, seven years is absolutely incredible. Last year he won, I think, all the individual awards you can win.

"And we're very proud to have him as captain. It's true that we're having conversations about his new contract, but I prefer to keep that private. I think it's something that needs to be discussed behind the scenes between him and the club."

articles.title: Bruno Fernandes: Man Utd trigger captain's one-year contract extension
articles.summary: Manchester United activate an option on captain Bruno Fernandes' contract, extending it until 2028.
articles.body:
Manchester United have triggered their one-year option on captain Bruno Fernandes' contract.

The 32-year-old's deal was due to expire next summer but sources say both parties decided it was in their best interests to activate the option through to 2028.

It means overseas clubs will not be able to approach Fernandes when the transfer window opens on 1 January.

The Portugal international confirmed on Tuesday that discussions over a new contract had been paused. Sources say they will resume once United's league position has improved.

Fernandes has made 343 appearances for United, scoring 115 goals, since his £47m move from Sporting in January 2020.

Last season he broke the Premier League assists record and scooped all of the individual player of the year awards after an outstanding campaign as United finished third.

While there is doubt over his long-term future, extending the contract means United would be able to command a fee for Fernandes should he leave in the summer.

United had been open to selling Fernandes in the summer of 2025, with Saudi Pro-League club Al Hilal offering a huge deal.

After discussing the situation with his wife, Fernandes decided to stay, though he later said it "hurt" United were willing to sell him. He reiterated on Tuesday he was still ambitious to win the biggest honours in the game.

Fernandes is a doubt for Saturday's Premier League encounter with Brentford after returning from the Champions League trip to Sporting with a virus.

The playmaker, who scored both goals in the 2-2 draw with his former club, but did not train on Friday and head coach Mauricio Pochettino said he would take a decision on his captain's fitness on Saturday morning.

"We are going to assess during the day and then tomorrow see how he is when he wakes up," said Pochettino. "We are not going to take any risks."

Pochettino was criticised by former Liverpool and England midfielder Jamie Redknapp on the Overlap earlier this week.

Reference was made to the former Tottenham, Paris St-Germain and Chelsea coach high-fiving Sky Sports reporter Patrick Davidson after his side's 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday, as evidence Pochettino had lost his edge.

"When I saw Pochettino at Southampton and I saw him at Tottenham, he looked like he had that Argentinian dog in him," said Redknapp.

"I look at him now and he's high-fiving everyone, he's got the bracelets on, he's got the barnet. I think he's gone too nice."

It seems someone had mentioned the observation to Pochettino as he went off on a tangent at his Friday news conference when asked about a "crazy" first week that included red cards, refereeing errors, disallowed goals and a drone filming training.

"What are we going to do? Start to cry?" he asked. "No. We have to be strong, believe and keep going. I cannot judge the past. Who am I to do that? I was in Cincinnati. I was outside. I need to shut my mouth, say nothing and start from now.

"Sometimes we are so confusing two words that means something similar; nice and good. I am not nice. We have to be good. It is a different thing. We know when we need to push, when we need to be strong, and when we need to build something to improve the atmosphere and relationship and everything.

Pochettino also confirmed £70m midfielder Carlos Baleba is expected to be out until the last week in January with the hamstring injury he sustained against Roma on 3 November.

Forward Marcus Rashford had begun to do individual work outside as he tries to recover from a hip problem that has kept him out since 13 October.

articles.title: End of 20-year partnership? Lionel Messi reportedly moves to ban AFA from using his name and image amid corruption probe
articles.summary: Lionel Messi reportedly moves to ban the Argentine Football Association (AFA) from using his name and image due to upcoming legal scrutiny and commercial disputes. Find out the implications for both the football star and the AFA as they navigate these troubling waters.
articles.body: Lionel Messi has spent two decades as the face of Argentine football, helping turn the national team into one of the most commercially recognisable brands in the sport. But that relationship could be changing. According to a report first published by Argentine newspaper Clarín on November 15, the Inter Miami forward has asked his legal team to prepare a cease-and-desist letter preventing the Argentine Football Association (AFA) from using his name and image for commercial purposes.Messi reportedly moves to distance himself from AFAAccording to Clarín, Messi had asked his legal representatives to prepare a cease-and-desist letter addressed to the AFA and its president, Claudio Tapia. The proposed legal notice would prevent the federation from using the footballer's image, name, photographs, and any audiovisual material recorded in different formats to generate revenue or business opportunities through his association, marking a significant change in a relationship that has benefited both parties for years.Messi has been the defining figure of Argentina's national team for approximately 20 years, with his image closely associated with the country's international football identity. The AFA has also expanded its commercial operations considerably, particularly after Argentina won the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.Its marketing strategy increasingly targeted international markets, including China, the Middle East and the United States, seeking to capitalise on the national team's global popularity. Messi's presence has been central to that appeal, although the 38-year-old has an enormous commercial identity independent of the federation.According to the report, Messi's decision would allow him to distance his personal brand from an organisation facing serious legal scrutiny. The report described the move as the beginning of commercial separation proceedings between the player and the AFA.There are conflicting reports over whether the letter has already been sent or is simply ready to go. So far, neither Messi nor the AFA has publicly commented on the matter.AFA corruption investigation and the VID Music Group lawsuitThe reported move comes as the AFA and Tapia face scrutiny over allegations of financial misconduct in Argentina. A Buenos Aires-based investigation is examining claims that millions of dollars connected to the federation's revenues dating back to 2023 were misappropriated.The investigation has reportedly involved police raids on AFA offices and properties allegedly owned by Tapia and his close associate, AFA lieutenant Pablo Toviggino. Authorities have also seized vehicles as part of inquiries into suspected financial irregularities.The AFA and Tapia have maintained their innocence, and Messi has not been named as a suspect in the corruption investigation.However, the forward has faced a separate legal dispute involving the federation. In April 2026, Messi and the AFA were sued by VID Music Group, a Miami-based events promoter, following a dispute over an international friendly between Argentina and Venezuela.The match was held at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens in October 2025. Messi did not feature in Argentina's 1-0 victory, instead watching from a private box with his family. VID alleged that it had paid for the accommodation and that his absence constituted a breach of contract.The lawsuit also accused Messi of conspiring with third-party agent Julian Marcos Kapelan to persuade the promoter to enter into agreements with the AFA under false pretences. The allegations included negligent misrepresentation and tortious interference with contract.According to The Athletic, being named alongside the AFA in the VID lawsuit may have been the final straw for Messi, but Clarín also pointed to a series of commercial disputes that had made the relationship increasingly difficult. The Argentine newspaper reported that the Messi family had dealt privately with complaints from prominent international sponsors over the federation's use of the player's image.One example involved an Argentine beer brand sponsoring the AFA that used Messi's image in a major advertising campaign during the 2022 World Cup. The problem was that Messi was already the face of American beer brand Michelob, forcing his family to explain the conflicting association directly to his sponsors after the campaign was launched without their agreement. Clarín described this as one of several similar incidents that had never previously been made public.The reported disputes suggest that Messi's concerns extended beyond the legal troubles surrounding Tapia and the federation, with the handling of his commercial image also becoming a source of friction.Argentina's commercial appeal without MessiThe reported disagreement also comes at a time when Argentina is experiencing the practical consequences of Messi's reduced involvement with the national team.Following his international retirement in September, the AFA organised a farewell appearance for the forward in October against Benin at River Plate's Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires. The match was arranged at short notice, but demand to see Messi in Argentina colours remained exceptionally high.According to Clarín, tickets were priced at approximately $60 and sold out within 90 minutes. They subsequently appeared on the secondary market, with resale prices reportedly exceeding $600, putting the farewell beyond the reach of many Argentine supporters.The contrast became apparent during Argentina's November friendlies against Uruguay and Costa Rica. The matches, played without Messi, attracted considerably smaller crowds despite the national team's continued popularity.Argentina faced Uruguay at La Bombonera before meeting Costa Rica at the Estadio Mario Alberto Kempes in Córdoba. Attendance was notably lower at both fixtures, with ticket prices remaining high despite the absence of the former captain.The situation was particularly visible during the Costa Rica match, when stadium officials opened the gates at half-time and allowed thousands of supporters to enter without paying.For the AFA, Messi's reported request to restrict the commercial use of his identity would create another challenge as it attempts to expand the national team's brand internationally. The federation's commercial ambitions have benefited enormously from his association with Argentina, particularly following the 2022 World Cup triumph.The distinction now is that Messi's personal brand is no longer necessarily aligned with the organisation's interests. If the reported cease-and-desist letter is formally issued and enforced, the AFA could lose the ability to use one of its most valuable commercial assets in the same way it has for much of the past two decades.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Scottish Premiership key issues: Falkirk chase seven in a row & Celtic visit Hearts
articles.summary: Falkirk's trip to Ibrox and Hearts' home match with Celtic stand out in another crucial Scottish Premiership weekend.
articles.body:
The Scottish Premiership rolls into town again this weekend with crucial games in both halves of the table.

Last week, Falkirk beat St Johnstone to secure six top-flight wins in a row for the first time since 1966.

Victory at Ibrox on Saturday would make it seven in a row in the highest Scottish league for the first time since 1907, during a season in which the Bairns finished second.

In order to do that, John McGlynn's side would have to become the first Falkirk team to win against Rangers at Ibrox since a 1994 League Cup tie when Richard Cadette scored twice in a 2-1 victory.

Falkirk are also looking to hold on to third place, with Hearts a point behind having played a game fewer.

However, Rangers have their own motivation, not least extending their 14-match unbeaten run in all competitions - a sequence that has included 12 wins.

By winning their game in hand against Aberdeen on Tuesday, Rangers moved to within a point of Premiership leaders and reigning champions Celtic.

Therefore, three points would take Rangers top before Celtic visit Hearts on Sunday.

Frick brings heavy metal football to Pittodrie

Two games in, Mario Frick's reign as Aberdeen head coach has produced 11 goals - six for, five against - and one win and one loss. Heavy metal football, as he promised.

Both were away from home - against Kilmarnock and Rangers - and on Saturday, Frick takes charge of a game at Pittodrie for the first time, with Dundee the visitors.

The Dons have won just twice at home in the Premiership this season, their last such victory coming in mid-October.

Dundee are still licking their wounds after last Saturday's 8-0 home defeat by Hearts and Tuesday's 2-1 loss away to Hibs.

Steven Pressley's side are on a three-match losing run after a promising start to the season.

Though they are not in any immediate danger of being dragged down towards the relegation zone, such a scenario may not be far away unless they arrest their current slide.

Four points separate St Johnstone in sixth and second bottom Motherwell.

Dundee are just below Saints on goal difference while three teams - Aberdeen, Hibernian and St Mirren - are a point above Well.

It's so tight and bottom side Kilmarnock, who visit St Mirren, are four points adrift and at risk of becoming detached.

This weekend's fixtures could make the order of the bottom seven look rather different come close of play on Saturday.

St Johnstone are away to fifth-placed Dundee United, but Aberdeen v Dundee, St Mirren v Kilmarnock and the evening meeting of Motherwell and Hibs at Fir Park pitch those congested sides up against one another.

Celtic in capital as Hearts seek redress

Celtic took only one point from last season's trips to Tynecastle but had the last laugh with victory over Hearts in Glasgow on the final day of the league season to tip Derek McInnes' side to the Premiership title.

McInnes' replacement Wouter Vrancken took his much-changed Hearts side to Celtic Park last month and were overrun in a 7-1 defeat, easily Celtic's best performance of the season so far.

Sunday is a chance for Hearts to atone for that loss and give Vrancken the sort of statement performance and win the home supporters are looking for.

Both sides had European fixtures on Thursday, with varying results.

Hearts were undone by a late goal in their 3-2 Conference League defeat at home to Monaco before Celtic boosted their hopes of Europa League progress with a 2-1 victory away to Portuguese side Torreense.

European hangovers notwithstanding, any goals would ensure an extension of no 0-0 draws between these sides since 2015.

articles.title: Arsenal vs Man City: What can Enzo Maresca's side learn from defensively strong Gunners?
articles.summary: Manchester City's leaky defence faces one of the most difficult games of the season with a trip to watertight Arsenal, aiming to put right their patchy recent form.
articles.body:
Manchester City 's leaky defence faces one of its most difficult tasks of the season with a trip to watertight Arsenal , aiming to put right their patchy recent form.

Enzo Maresca's side began the season with eight straight victories but have won only one of their past seven in all competitions inside 90 minutes and head to Emirates Stadium trailing the champions by six points even at this early juncture.

A Premier League defeat on Sunday could well have long-term consequences for City's title aspirations, with Mikel Arteta's men clearly standing above any other top-flight side as the ones to topple.

Though the Gunners dropped points last weekend with a draw at Newcastle , they continue to set the standards with a miserly defence that has conceded only seven goals in the club's opening 11 league games.

Asked why he felt City have dropped off in recent weeks, Maresca - who replaced Pep Guardiola as manager in the summer - said: "For me it's because we've had four months together. Transition requires time.

"It's probably because we won seven games in a row, with Champions League eight in a row. Everyone was thinking at City there's no transition but I've said many times I am not a magician. There is transition, it's normal.

"There are eight or nine new players, the manager is new so you need time and you can see different clubs when they had transition how complicated it is. For me, it's completely normal, I'm completely relaxed, no panic at all."

'Pass, pass, slow, slow' - Man City's slick machine grinding to a halt

Why Man City can't wear their new kit in Premier League

"We are conceding too many goals and we need to avoid that," was an obvious statement made by Maresca following last Saturday's 1-1 draw against Fulham.

City followed that up with another home stalemate against Napoli in the Champions League on Tuesday and have now conceded in 10 successive games in all competitions for the first time in seven years.

"[It was] far, far too easy to play through [City]," said former England captain Alan Shearer of Rodrigo Muniz's goal for Fulham on Match of the Day.

" Fulham 's throw-in was level with their own 18-yard box. For them to get through is not acceptable at any level, let alone when you are playing for Manchester City and Muniz ran past the entire midfield [to score]."

City have managed only five clean sheets all campaign, which is in stark contrast to Arsenal , who have kept double the amount so far, while Newcastle 's opening goal ended a run off 445 minutes without the ball hitting their net.

Maresca's men also have an issue by conceding the opener, having done so seven times in the past 10 games, and of the 14 goals they have shipped, six have come inside the first 20 minutes.

An early Arsenal goal may well be an important factor in deciding Sunday's contest.

Asked how his side can improve defensively, Maresca said: "Video [analysis], meetings, [on] pitch coaching, It is a mix of that.

"Some of the goals we concede we can avoid, so hopefully we can do that."

The injury to key defender William Saliba has almost gone unnoticed for Arsenal as Ezri Konsa has stepped in to fill the void at centre-back seamlessly since joining from Aston Villa in the summer.

The England international has established a formidable partnership with Gabriel and the two have quickly formed an impressive understanding this season.

Maresca, meanwhile, admitted he was still "trying to find different" solutions to his team, which has been highlighted by the chopping and changing of his backline.

In 16 Premier League and Champions League games this season, the Italian has used eight different combinations in defence, which has given players little chance of fostering any sort of on-pitch relationships with each other.

City have also made seven errors leading to goals, compared to Arsenal 's one.

"You are concerned in some way because that is a lot of errors leading to goals," said former City defender Nedum Onuoha. "With some of the best players you ask, 'what are they really good at?' For some it is the fact they don't make mistakes.

"They are ruthless and relentless in the way they play but at this moment in time City are being punished for those errors.

"A manager can have the tactics and do the team talks, but if people are going to continue to make those mistakes, they will suffer."

The chant of "1-0 to the Arsenal " has been synonymous with the Gunners over the years and it could not be more apt under Arteta.

Since the start of last season, his side have won 16 matches in all competitions by that particular scoreline, compared to six by City.

After beating Sunderland in a chaotic match in September, Maresca said he would "prefer to win 1-0 than 5-3", suggesting his side needed more control and he re-iterated that message after the Fulham draw.

"Sometimes you need to win games 1-0 for a small difference and to keep a clean sheet but in this moment we are not able to do that," he admitted.

City, though, have scored five more league goals than Arsenal in this campaign and Sunday's hosts have injury concerns over goalkeeper David Raya.

The Spaniard is a doubt with the shoulder problem he picked up at Newcastle , and compatriot Kepa Arrizabalaga may deputise again as he did in the 1-1 draw against Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League on Tuesday.

City have fond memories of coming up against Arsenal 's stand-in keeper, after Kepa's howler for the opening goal contributed to their 2-0 Carabao Cup final triumph back in March.

A repeat result on Sunday will provide a much-needed morale boost for Maresca and his team.

articles.title: Erling Haaland ‘happy’ at Man City despite transfer talk, says Maresca
articles.summary: Erling Haaland blasted beleaguered City’s form, but ahead of Arsenal test, manager Enzo Maresca says striker is happy.
articles.body:
Enzo Maresca insisted on Friday that Erling Haaland is “happy” at Manchester City after the striker expressed frustration over his side’s recent struggles.

Haaland gave a candid assessment of City’s malaise following Tuesday’s 2-2 draw against Napoli in the Champions League, which came on the back of a Premier League draw at home with Fulham.

After winning 10 of their first 11 matches in all competitions this season, Maresca’s men have won just two of their last seven.

With a crucial trip to Premier League leaders Arsenal looming on Sunday, Haaland’s criticism added to the growing sense that City’s season is in danger of spiralling out of control.

“We have to do better and find some ways to control the game more and perform in a better way,” Haaland said.

“I have no idea what we were missing but you could feel it in the last few games that something was not clicking fully.”

Haaland has scored just once in his last five games for City and is without a league goal in his past three matches.

The Norway star’s body language has been noticeably angst-ridden in recent weeks, prompting suggestions that he is growing disillusioned with life at the Etihad Stadium.

City are also awaiting the result of their appeal against a guilty verdict over breaches of Premier League financial rules, with the punishment potentially including a huge points deduction.

Despite City’s woes, Maresca is adamant Haaland remains committed to the cause regardless of speculation that he could seek a move at the end of the season.

“Erling is a nine; they live for goals and winning games. If they don’t score, they are upset. I think he gesticulates in the same way when we are winning games,” Maresca told reporters on Friday.

“For sure he is not happy because we are not winning games. But it is not just Erling. Everyone is on the same page.

“He has been good. He has been normal since day one. Two or three weeks ago, he was dancing inside the pitch and in the training sessions.

“He is happy. It is normal that results affect the mood a little bit but I don’t see any problem with Erling. He is a winner.”

Maresca will need Haaland back to his best against Arsenal if third-placed City are to earn a vital victory over the champions.

Already trailing six points behind Arsenal, a defeat in north London would be a huge blow to their title hopes.

Maresca has come under fire during City’s slump in his first season after replacing Pep Guardiola.

The former Chelsea boss claimed teething problems were inevitable during the transition from Guardiola’s dynastic reign.

“Transition requires time. It’s probably because we won seven games in a row, everyone was thinking at City there’s no transition,” Maresca said.

“But I’ve said many times I’m not a magician. There are eight or nine new players, the manager is new.

“For sure, when you don’t win games, it’s not the ideal situation. For me, it’s completely normal, I’m completely relaxed, no panic at all.”

articles.title: Renee Slegers leaves Arsenal only 18 months after winning Champions League following poor start to WSL season
articles.summary: Renee Slegers leaves Arsenal after less than two years in charge; Slegers led Gunners to Women's Champions League title in May 2025, but exits after poor start to 2026/27 campaign; the Gunners sit sixth in the WSL, 12 points off the top and have not won at home in the league all season
articles.body:
Slegers led Arsenal to Women's Champions League glory in May 2025 , having initially stepped up from assistant to Jonas Eidevall on an interim basis, then narrowly missed out on the WSL title to Manchester City in 2025/26.

Such was her success at the time, the Dutchwoman signed a new contract with the club in January 2026, running until 2029.

But a poor start to the 2026/27 campaign, in which Arsenal went on a five-game winless run in the WSL for the first time in their history, has culminated in Slegers' departure just 10 months into her new deal.

The Gunners remain winless at home in the WSL this season having drawn a sixth consecutive game against West Ham on Sunday.

Arsenal sit sixth in the WSL, 12 points off leaders Chelsea and eight points behind London City Lionesses in the third and final Champions League position.

Slegers' side have also only scored 11 goals in 11 WSL matches this season - only Everton and bottom club Charlton have managed fewer this term.

Her assistant coach Aaron D'Antino - who has been with the Gunners since 2018 - also leaves the club, with former Brighton boss and current Arsenal head of analytics Melissa Clarke-Reed taking interim charge.

"It was an extremely difficult decision to part ways with Renee, who has led the team with dedication and commitment throughout her time here," said director of women's football Clare Wheatley.

"In leading us to glory in the Champions League and the inaugural FIFA Champions Cup, Renee has made a significant and lasting contribution to the history of Arsenal Football Club, with close support from Aaron.

"After careful reflection, it is clear that results have been below the expected level, and change is necessary."

Analysis from Sky Sports News' Anton Toloui : "It's been described to me as a sad day at Arsenal. The club did not want to have to make this decision, but results this season have dictated Renee Slegers' future, and they have had to make the difficult choice to let her go.

"Richard Garlick, the club's CEO, informed staff just before 3pm, and director of football Claire Wheatley has been ringing round the players, most of whom are on international duty, to let them know that Slegers won't be there when they come back to the club.

"It's a difficult time. They went into the season as narrow favourites to end their title WSL drought - they haven't won the competition since 2019. But this season, the results have not lived up to the hype, despite the fact they went on a big summer recruitment drive, bringing in the likes of Georgia Stanway, Misa Rodriguez, and Ona Batlle.

"Arsenal currently sit sixth in the table, six draws from six home games in the league so far. Only three wins in the competition sees them way off the title hunt, maybe even outsiders to make it into the Champions League this season.

"But Slegers leaves the club with a lot of love after taking over from Jonas Eidevall, lifting up the spirits and bringing the club their first Champions League trophy for 18 years."

'Lack of WSL title challenge part of decision'

Analysis from Sky Sports News' Uma Gurav: "It was one of those decisions that felt like it was coming, particularly after the last set of games that Arsenal have played.

"This follows Arsenal's 0-0 draw with West Ham at the Emirates last weekend and what's so significant about that is it means Arsenal are yet to win at home in the WSL this season, a place that used to be their fortress.

"Now, it's a place where so many teams have come and taken points off them.

"It just didn't look like a coherent Arsenal team on Sunday. Players were coming off in tears and it means they have a lot of work to do to get anything out of this season.

"At the moment, they are eight points off those Champions League places. They wanted to win the WSL this season - that hasn't happened and I think that's partly why this decision has been taken.

"Arsenal have got three more games before Christmas, all away games at Everton and Charlton in the WSL and then one against Inter Milan to see what they can salvage so far from this block of games.

"When we return from the international break, it will be a new Arsenal, with a new team in charge. Let's see if they can turn their season around."

December 11 - Everton (a), WSL, live on Sky Sports Premier League

December 16 - Inter (a), Women's Champions League

December 20 - Charlton (a), WSL, live on Sky Sports

articles.title: Renee Slegers has left Arsenal by mutual consent - how her tenure went from hero to zero in such a short space of time
articles.summary: Renee Slegers has left Arsenal after two years in charge; for a tenure that started so spectacularly, things have gone sour at a rapid rate; Sky Sports' Laura Hunter analyses how did the Dutchwomen's position became untenable
articles.body:
Slegers' impact was instantaneous when she assumed control of Arsenal back in October 2024, initially on an interim basis. Stepping up to take over from Jonas Eidevall, previously his assistant, was seamless. She already knew the squad. The squad were just as familiar with her. The fit was perfect.

Slegers took a side on the slide to the zenith of the women's game within seven months. Beating Barcelona on a barmy night in Lisbon to lift the Champions League trophy, the only English club ever to do so, was a triumph few would have considered possible when she took the role. Slegers described it as "above all expectations".

The root of her success was an open secret. Calm and composed but equally candid, Slegers' authority was built on a transparency that previously never existed. There was trust, accountability and mutual respect. As a collective, Arsenal's bond was their greatest asset.

So, how has such strength of sentiment been lost?

Arsenal's squad was once filled with stalwarts of the game. Some still remain, but the nucleus of the group has begun to move towards a younger, more dynamic composition. There is a lot of talent.

But perhaps Arsenal lost a bit of personality when they allowed both Katie McCabe and Beth Mead to leave in the same summer - to join direct WSL rivals. Those decisions were footballing ones, and yet, it feels like the soul of the club, those who understand and embody what it is to be Arsenal, is lacking.

They also let Victoria Pelova move across north London to Spurs, only to emerge as one of the league's top scorers. The 27-year-old, at peak age, has a better goals per 90 ratio than any Arsenal player this term - including Alessia Russo - and the best striking accuracy of any midfielder in the division.

With the benefit of hindsight, it's difficult to view any of those outgoings as helpful to Arsenal's cause.

Slegers has failed to find a balanced formula this season, criticised for using key players in unfamiliar positions. Right-back Ona Batlle has spent all campaign at left-back. Russo has played nearly 40 per cent of her total league minutes as a No 10.

The composition of the back four changes every game. Leah Williamson has had three different centre-back partners, none of which have stuck. And the full-back positions rotate weekly. In total, Slegers has fielded six different defensive arrangements across 11 games.

Her total starting XI changes amount to 29, which is not unusual given the size of Arsenal's squad. Chelsea have made 31. But a lack of consistency is not helping a team under pressure. Nor have in-game tactical adjustments been able to flip a result frequently enough.

Olivia Smith is the only player to have scored a goal as a substitute all season, rescuing a draw against newly-promoted Birmingham in October. Such limited impact from a squad of Arsenal's size reflects most damningly on those in charge of its deployment.

It is no secret that Arsenal cannot break down a compact defence. It's been a systematic failing that pre-dates Slegers - but has worsened. Opposition teams travel to the Emirates and set up for a point, almost always leaving with one.

Arsenal have no problem establishing territorial dominance because the squad is filled with ball-players but once in the final third, a lack of penetration means they struggle to manipulate deep defensive shapes. Possession ends with a predictable cross or a shot into traffic.

Russo's threat remains but she has no creative support. She is Plan A, B and C. That tactical inertia is harming Arsenal's chances of winning games, especially at the Emirates, where expectant home crowds demand more than six consecutive draws containing a frugal four goals.

Arsenal's conversion rate from chances created and shots on target is at an all-time low. Their latest goalless stalemate with West Ham saw their conversion percentage at home plummet to just 2.8. More than a problem, it's a pattern.

An atmosphere that was once the great envy of the league has gone stale. Perhaps that is the clearest symptom of Slegers' stagnation.

Last season Arsenal won eight of their 11 home games. Slegers actually maintained an unbeaten record in the league at home, but drawing all six Emirates outings this year led fans to turn sour - or not turn up at all. Attendances are down and the shift in mood is hardly subtle.

There is no vibe to Arsenal in this context. Hoping they eventually revert to type no longer feels sufficient given how much evidence there is to the contrary. Every home performance is a repeat of the one that went before it: forced and faceless. Main character energy has long faded.

Six home draws cannot be considered freak variance. It's a cycle opposition teams have learned to use against them.

A final nail in the coffin concerns how far Arsenal have fallen away from challenging for domestic honours. Spurs are five points better off in the position ahead. Man City are 10 clear. And the gap to leaders Chelsea is 12.

Arsenal had a foundation from which to build after a European triumph no one planned or expected. It was a gift. But the club have allowed that momentum to fizzle into nothingness.

This is a team in decline; a change of leaders was unavoidable.

Analysis from Sky Sports News' Anton Toloui : "It's been described to me as a sad day at Arsenal. The club did not want to have to make this decision, but results this season have dictated Renee Slegers' future, and they have had to make the difficult choice to let her go.

"Richard Garlick, the club's CEO, informed staff just before 3pm, and director of football Claire Wheatley has been ringing round the players, most of whom are on international duty, to let them know that Slegers won't be there when they come back to the club.

"It's a difficult time. They went into the season as narrow favourites to end their title WSL drought - they haven't won the competition since 2019. But this season, the results have not lived up to the hype, despite the fact they went on a big summer recruitment drive, bringing in the likes of Georgia Stanway, Misa Rodriguez, and Ona Batlle.

"Arsenal currently sit sixth in the table, six draws from six home games in the league so far. Only three wins in the competition sees them way off the title hunt, maybe even outsiders to make it into the Champions League this season.

"But Slegers leaves the club with a lot of love after taking over from Jonas Eidevall, lifting up the spirits and bringing the club their first Champions League trophy for 18 years."

articles.title: Manchester United trigger Bruno Fernandes contract extension to 2028
articles.summary: The captain had said that a long-term contract renewal was on hold, but Premier League club exercised one-year option.
articles.body:
Manchester United are understood to have extended Bruno Fernandes’ existing contract by 12 months, ending speculation about a pre-contract agreement with an overseas club.

The Professional Football Association’s Player of the Year was in the final year of his existing contract, which would have allowed him to speak with clubs outside the Premier League from January 1 about a move next summer.

Fernandes had revealed that negotiations about a new contract had been put on hold , adding to speculation that he could seek a move away from a team that are currently in the league relegation zone.

United, however, are understood to have triggered a clause in the current deal to keep Fernandes at the Old Trafford club until the end of the 2027-2028 season.

Fernandes joined United in January 2020 from Sporting Lisbon, against whom he scored twice in the two sides’ midweek Champions League 2-2 draw .

The attacking midfielder quickly became the club’s most important player and last season performed a record number of assists in a Premier League season, helping secure the return to Europe’s elite competition for this campaign.

A team source said the move suited both parties and left the door open to future talks over a ⁠⁠new contract, although the immediate priority was improving results.

United are languishing in 19th place in the Premier League after their worst start to a top-flight season in 40 years.

Fernandes a doubt for Manchester United against Brentford

United entertain Brentford in the Premier League on Saturday, marking new manager Mauricio Pochettino’s first home game in charge of the club.

Fernandes, however, is a doubt for the match after missing training on Friday due to illness.

“We don’t know,” Pochettino said on Friday when asked if Fernandes will play. “He’s affected by a virus from Portugal. He finished the game a little bit with a problem and today he could not be part of the training session.”

“We’ll see during the day and [Saturday] how he wakes up. We’re not going to take any risks. When this type of situation happens, you don’t feel right. We are ⁠⁠going to pay attention, but still we have decided nothing.”

Pochettino is still searching for his first victory after the dramatic draw in Lisbon and a 4-0 ⁠⁠Premier League thrashing by Liverpool last weekend, although United were encouraged by their improved display in Portugal.

“We arrive full of energy, ⁠⁠positive, but it’s difficult for the players when the results ⁠⁠haven’t been up to scratch. We try to help them as best we can,” Pochettino said of his first week in charge.

“This is a group of players who want to do well, who want to perform. Our ‌‌job is to build confidence.”

On the speculation that had been swirling around Fernandes’ future in Manchester, following reports he had turned down two new contract offers, the Portugal midfielder said on Tuesday ‌‌that ‌‌talks could wait until results improve.

“I’m more worried about getting results, trying to bring the club back in a position to be proud of,” he said.

articles.title: Renee Slegers: Arsenal head coach leaves by mutual consent
articles.summary: Arsenal part company with head coach Renee Slegers by mutual consent after a disappointing start to the season.
articles.body:
Arsenal have parted company with head coach Renee Slegers by mutual consent after a disappointing start to the season.

Slegers, 37, was initially appointed on an interim basis in October 2024 before being handed the role permanently three months later.

The Dutchwoman led Arsenal to their second Women's Champions League title in May 2025 and the inaugural Fifa Women's Champions Cup in February 2026.

But she leaves with the team sixth in the Women's Super League after 11 matches - 12 points behind leaders Chelsea.

Assistant coach Aaron D'Antino has also left the club, with assistant Melissa Clarke-Reed placed in interim charge as they begin the search for a permanent replacement.

D'Antino had been part of Arsenal's coaching staff since August 2018.

Arsenal director of women's football Clare Wheatley said the decision had been "extremely difficult".

"In leading us to glory in the Champions League and the inaugural Fifa Champions Cup, Renee has made a significant and lasting contribution to the history of Arsenal Football Club, with close support from Aaron," she said.

"After careful reflection, it is clear that results have been below the expected level, and change is necessary."

Chief executive Richard Garlick paid tribute to both departing coaches, describing Slegers as "a wonderful person" who had played "an integral role in some of the most historic achievements in the club's history".

"Our ambition is to compete for and win major trophies consistently, and our recent results have led us to conclude that a change is necessary to give us the best opportunity to achieve those goals," he added.

Why Arsenal are behind in race for Champions League spots

Pressure was building for weeks - analysis

Slegers' departure comes after weeks of pressure as Arsenal's WSL form continued to deteriorate.

While the Dutch coach delivered the Women's Champions League and Women's Champions Cup, results in the league have fallen below expectations this season.

Arsenal have endured a four-match winless run in the league and their struggles have been particularly stark at their own Emirates Stadium, where they have gone six matches without a victory.

For a side expected to challenge for major trophies every season, those dropped points are damaging as they have fallen well adrift of Chelsea and even eight points behind London City Lionesses, who are in the third Women's Champions League qualification spot.

A lack of goals has been central to Arsenal's struggles. They have scored just 11 times in 11 WSL matches this season - less than half the tally of Chelsea (29), second-placed Manchester City (28) and London City Lionesses (31).

Before Slegers' exit was confirmed on Friday, former Arsenal and England forward Lianne Sanderson had called for the manager to depart.

"I've been a big advocate for Renee to stay in the job, but after the Lyon game [a 2-0 home defeat in the Champions League], I felt this feeling in my stomach that it's time [to part ways]," Sanderson told FourFourTwo , external .

"That was probably the most defeated I have felt. The players weren't fighting, they had just shown nothing, there was no identity.

"The definition of insanity is doing the same thing over and over again and expecting different results."

After Sunday's draw with West Ham, Slegers acknowledged performances and results had fallen short of expectations and made it clear she accepted responsibility.

"I love the club," she said. "We're going through a very, very difficult time, and I take my responsibilities, because the results haven't been good enough.

"In the second half we are chasing again, but we're not creating good enough chances to the final third, from all phases, and the way we get there, it's not the Arsenal standard and we need to do that better.

"But I take my responsibilities in my role."

articles.title: Savio: Tottenham winger set to miss Christmas fixtures after injury setback
articles.summary: Tottenham winger Savio will miss the club's Christmas fixtures with injury and could be out for up to 80 days, manager Roberto de Zerbi confirms.
articles.body:
Tottenham winger Savio will miss the club's Christmas fixtures with injury and could be out for up to 80 days, manager Roberto de Zerbi has confirmed.

Savio joined Spurs from Manchester City for £75m this summer, but has played in just five of their 11 Premier League matches this season.

The 22-year-old came on as a substitute in the 64th minute of Tottenham 's 2-0 win over Ipswich on Saturday, but was forced off with two minutes remaining with a hamstring injury.

It was the attacker's first game back in six weeks after returning from a muscle problem which led to him missing the four previous league matches.

Asked if Savio, previously known as Savinho, would miss the Christmas schedule, De Zerbi said: "Yes, I think so unfortunately.

"It is a tough situation to accept. He is a good guy. He is suffering for this new injury but it is part of football."

"If you see the other European clubs, all of them, they are suffering many, many injuries."

Savio is still searching for his first league goal or assist for Tottenham , although he did score and assist a goal on his debut in August in a 5-1 win over Charlton in the Carabao Cup.

"Now, he needs time and hard work with the medical staff," De Zerbi added.

"Then in 50, 60 or 80 days - I don't know when he comes back - he'll be crucial for us for the last step of the season."

Tottenham are 10th in the league and have won four of their past five matches after a poor start to the season.

They travel to 18th-placed Sunderland on Sunday (14:05 GMT).

articles.title: Los clubes de la Premier quieren obligar al dueño del City a venderlo
articles.standfirst: El regulador independiente tiene la potestad de forzar la venta en casos graves de infracción
articles.summary: El regulador independiente tiene la potestad de forzar la venta en casos graves de infracción
articles.body: El proceso contra el Manchester City avanza y las noticias son poco alentadoras para el conjunto sky blue. Lo último que publica BBC es una amenaza directa a la propiedad del club. "Los propietarios del Manchester City deben verse obligados a vender el club como castigo por incumplir las normas financieras. Directivos de tres clubes de primera división han declarado a la BBC que creen que este es el castigo apropiado para el City", cuenta el medio inglés. Ante las amenazas de retirada de la inversión de Emiratos Árabes Unidos en Reino Unido, David Kogan, el presidente de la IFR, la comisión independiente encargada de examinar el caso y sancionar al City, asegura que no se va a dejar influir por ninguna presión política: "Olvidemos el nombre del club, olvidemos su tamaño, olvidemos la magnitud del problema. No podemos simplemente ignorar nuestras obligaciones legales con respecto a un club sólo porque tenga un tamaño determinado". En el texto de BBC se desvela que "un ejecutivo, que habló bajo condición de anonimato, afirmó pertenecer a un grupo de clubes que consideran que la sanción al City será irrelevante a menos que los propietarios también se vean obligados a vender". Ese, sumado al eventual castigo en puntos que pueda recibir el City, sería considerado como "justo" por los rivales del club de Mánchester, que quieren forzar un cambio de propiedad en el Etihad. Según el calendario planteado hace un par de semanas por el Financial Times, la apelación tendrá lugar a mediados de diciembre y, una vez que la comisión decida sobre la apelación del club citizen, algo que sucederá a principios de enero, la sanción se podría hacer pública de manera casi inmediata. Eso sí, insistía el Financial Times, no está claro cuándo entrarían en vigor unos castigos que, además, serían apelables, lo que alargaría aún más un proceso que ya lleva años enturbiando el fútbol inglés.

articles.title: Jude Bellingham wins hearts with ‘life-changing’ gesture after tracking down photographer behind iconic celebration photo to give credit
articles.summary: Real Madrid star Jude Bellingham tracks down a photographer to credit him for a stunning image capturing his celebration, highlighting the importance of recognizing creators in sports.
articles.body: Jude Bellingham has become accustomed to having his own moments captured by cameras, but the Real Madrid midfielder made sure the person behind one particularly striking photograph received some recognition. After spotting an image of his celebration at the Bernabeu, the England international tracked down the photographer, thanked him privately and promised to credit his work before sharing it with millions of followers.Bellingham tracks down photographer before sharing viral celebration pictureBellingham was one of the standout performers in Real Madrid's 5-1 Champions League victory over PSV Eindhoven on Tuesday, scoring a superb goal and setting up another after coming on at half-time.With Madrid trailing 1-0 when he entered the match, Federico Valverde restored parity before Bellingham put the Spanish side ahead in the 60th minute with a spectacular volley. He later assisted Vinicius Junior as Madrid extended their advantage, while Kylian Mbappe scored twice in the emphatic victory.After finding the net, Bellingham celebrated in his trademark fashion, standing with his arms outstretched in front of the Bernabeu supporters. The pose was replicated by hundreds of fans in the stands, creating an impressive scene that photographer Mark Verhees managed to capture.The photograph showed Bellingham from behind in his white Real Madrid No. 5 shirt, facing a packed stand of supporters dressed predominantly in white, many of them mirroring his outstretched-arm celebration.Verhees uploaded the image to Instagram, where it subsequently caught the attention of the midfielder. Rather than simply saving the photograph and posting it on his own account, Bellingham made an effort to locate its original creator and contact him directlyIn an Instagram direct message, the England international wrote:“Hi mate, finally tracked down the original of the picture. Just wanted to say thank you for capturing such an amazing moment. I'm gonna upload it and tag you. Thanks again.”Verhees responded warmly, writing: “Of course, brother. It's a pleasure. Thank you for the love.”Bellingham subsequently shared the photograph on his Instagram account on Thursday evening, tagging the photographer and giving him credit for the image. The post attracted more than 3.7 million likes, with several of his Real Madrid teammates, including Vinicius Jr and Thibaut Courtois, also leaving comments.Fans praise Bellingham for recognising photographer's workThe exchange became even more widely shared after Verhees posted a screenshot of their private conversation on his Instagram story, allowing supporters to see how the midfielder had approached him.The response was overwhelmingly positive, with several fans highlighting the importance of acknowledging photographers whose work is frequently circulated across social media without proper credit.One supporter, identifying themselves as a photographer, wrote: “As a photographer, I can’t even describe how respectful this is of Bellingham to do. It takes seconds to credit somebody of their work, and this will potentially change the creators life too.”Another commented: “He’s changed that photographer’s life forever.”A third added: “Imagine being this polite when you literally have everything.”A fourth supporter, who said they had worked in the industry for more than 25 years, wrote: “Having worked in the industry for over 25 years, this is class from Jude. Bet the photographer was buzzing.”Another fan highlighted how easily the original creator of an image can be overlooked when photographs are shared online.“Here’s to more of this. So many photos on social media (and probably guilty of it myself) used without thinking about or crediting who the photographer is. I’ve not met Jude Bellingham but he does appear to have the simple quality of good manners.”The attention surrounding the exchange was not simply about the number of likes Bellingham's photograph received. By finding Verhees before publishing the image, thanking him and promising to tag him, the midfielder ensured that the person responsible for capturing the moment received recognition from an audience far larger than his own.Another considerate gesture after standing up for female reporterThe photographer exchange comes shortly after Bellingham received similar praise for his conduct during post-match media duties following the same victory over PSV.BBC Sport reporter Elizabeth Conway had asked the midfielder what had gone through his mind when he scored his remarkable volley. After Bellingham answered, Conway attempted to ask a second question but was interrupted by another journalist trying to get his own question in.Bellingham immediately stepped in, saying: “Sorry, she's got one more.”He then allowed Conway to finish asking whether he felt he was in the best form of his career for both club and country. The midfielder responded by explaining that his focus remained on preparing for the next match rather than dwelling on individual performances.Conway later shared the exchange on Instagram, writing: “Just Jude waiting for me to finish my questions.”The BBC also shared the footage on X, joking: “Jude Bellingham with his second assist of the night.”The reporter subsequently explained that mixed-zone interviews at Real Madrid could be intimidating, particularly for one of the few female and English journalists regularly covering the club. She described the environment as crowded and competitive, making Bellingham's decision to intervene particularly appreciated.His latest interaction with Verhees has brought another example of the midfielder recognising the people working around the game. Between giving a journalist the opportunity to finish her question and ensuring a photographer received credit for his work, Bellingham has attracted attention for gestures that took little time but meant considerably more to the people involved.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Olmo: "Tenemos un objetivo claro: ganar todo hasta el parón"
articles.standfirst: El catalán inauguró una Cruyff Court en su Terrassa natal
articles.summary: El catalán inauguró una Cruyff Court en su Terrassa natal
articles.body: Dani Olmo, junto a la la Fundación Johan Cruyff y Action, inauguraron este viernes por la tarde un Cruyff Court en Terrassa, localidad natal del internacional. El futbolista catalán apadrinó la puesta de largo junto a Susila Cruyff, presidenta de la Fundación Johan Cruyff; Pati Roura, directora de la Fundación Johan Cruyff; Francisco Nuñez Aparicio, General Manager Action Spain; y Jordi Ballart, alcalde de la ciudad egarense. "Siempre es especial inaugurar cosas en mi ciudad, Terrassa. Ya dije cuando celebramos el título del mundial en el Ayuntamiento que quedaba pendiente esta inauguración y, por fin, ahora los niños y niñas lo podrán disfrutar. Les he dicho que yo también empecé en la calle jugando, en los parques....", explicó el catalán. Dani Olmo aseguró que ya está al cien por cien tras dejar atrás la lesión que le mantuvo un mes fuera de los terrenos de juego. El catalán reconoció la importancia de encadenar éxitos antes de marcharse de vacaciones de Navidad. "Tenemos un objetivo claro: ganar todo hasta el parón y así poder descansar bien. Sabemos que esta Liga va a ser complicada, como cada año. Hay muchos partidos, pero tenemos plantilla de sobra para descansar y estar al cien por cien en todos los encuentros. Llevamos muy buena dinámica y ese es nuestro objetivo. Llevamos dos títulos de LaLiga consecutivos", recordó. Sobre los rumores que surgieron hace ya varias semanas acerca del interés del Bayern de Múnich, el internacional se mostró firme y reiteró su compromiso con el Barcelona. "Ya lo he dicho en más de una ocasión: estoy donde quiero estar. Hace dos años y medio ya dije que mi sueño y mi objetivo eran ganar títulos con el Barça. Quiero ganar más y devolver al Barça al lugar que se merece a nivel europeo", aseguró. Por último, también quiso referirse a la actualidad social y deportiva. Sobre la retirada de Marc Márquez, Dani Olmo se deshizo en elogios hacia el piloto. "Es una leyenda de las motos. Su manera de competir es ejemplar. Se va uno de los más grandes, pero su legado siempre será recordado". Por otro lado, no quiso pronunciarse sobre las elecciones del domingo. "Cada uno tiene su opinión y es libre. ¿Si he votado? Me lo reservo", concluyó. Las Cruyff Court tienen como objetivo ser un lugar de encuentro seguro y donde los niños y niñas conozcan la importancia de la unión, de hacer amistades, de descubrir su propio talento y de aprender a ganar y también a perder. Un conjunto de experiencias que contribuyen positivamente en su crecimiento, tanto físico como mental. En los últimos años, muchos jugadores del Barcelona han inaugurado estos campos en sus ciudades natales como Eric García (Martorell), Gerard Martín (Sant Andreu de la Barca), Jordi Alba, (L'Hospitalet).... Ahora se suma la de Dani Olmo, en Terrassa.

articles.title: Emery se 'reconcilia' con Garnacho: "Está entrenando muy bien y su actitud es fantástica"
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Aston Villa resta importancia a su ausencia en Champions ante el Galatasaray
articles.summary: El técnico del Aston Villa resta importancia a su ausencia en Champions ante el Galatasaray
articles.body: Unai Emery, técnico del Aston Villa, no ha cerrado la puerta a que Alejandro Garnacho vuelva a jugar con el equipo después de que el argentino se quedara fuera de la convocatoria de la Liga de Campeones y borrara sus fotos con el Aston Villa en redes sociales. Garnacho, cedido esta temporada por el United, apenas ha disputado 92 minutos con los 'villanos' repartido en siete encuentros, y el martes se quedó fuera de la convocatoria contra el Galatasaray, pese a que Emery tenía hueco para incluirle al menos en el banquillo. Esto, unido a que Garnacho ha borrado toda traza de su paso por el Villa en redes sociales, ha despertado los rumores del distanciamiento con el jugador argentino. "Alejandro está entrenando muy bien y su actitud es fantástica. Al principio de temporada le costaba, porque no estaba en forma. Ahora lo está. Está entrenando bien, pero el equipo está progresando, y cuando no le incluyo en el equipo es porque tengo que elegir a otros jugadores", explicó el técnico vasco en rueda de prensa. "Tiene mi respeto tanto primero como persona como segundo como jugador, pero no ha participado por esta razón. Eso sí, el fútbol puede cambiar. Es noviembre y claro que está la ventana de fichajes en enero, pero no estamos pensando en ello. Estamos jugando muchos partidos y necesitaremos jugadores. Ahora no está, pero está trabajando bien. Está al nivel que esperábamos de él al principio de temporada", insiste Emery. En Premier League, en los últimos ocho partidos, Garnacho sólo ha jugado tres minutos.

The No. 2 Utah Utes will face the No. 11 Texas Tech Red Raiders in the 2026 Edward Jones Big 12 Football Championship at 8 p.m. ET on Friday, December 4 at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas.

The game will air on ABC, but it can also be watched on the ESPN app, ESPN+, Fubo, and DIRECTV.

Utah has been one of the most surprising teams in college football this season. First-year head coach Morgan Scalley and star quarterback Devon Dampier have led the Utes to the only undefeated record in college football after a regular season that was full of upsets. They will enter Friday's season finale against West Virginia with a perfect 11-0 record.

Six different teams have won the Big 12 championship in the last six years, but Texas Tech is looking to become back-to-back conference champions after winning its first conference title in 70 years last season. The feat was last accomplished by Oklahoma, who won the title in 2019 and 2020. The Red Raiders finished the 2026 season with an 11-1 record. Their lone loss came against the Cincinnati Bearcats in late October.

The matchup will be the final iteration of the conference title game before the arrival of a 24-team College Football Playoff bracket eliminates conference championships next year.

articles.title: Alejandro Garnacho: Unai Emery praises Aston Villa winger after selection snub
articles.summary: Aston Villa boss Unai Emery praises Alejandro Garnacho's "fantastic attitude" but suggests other players rank ahead of him for selection.
articles.body:
Aston Villa boss Unai Emery has praised Alejandro Garnacho's "fantastic attitude" -but suggested other players rank ahead of him after the Argentine was left out of Tuesday's Champions League defeat at Galatasaray.

The 22-year-old winger joined Aston Villa on loan from Chelsea in the summer, but he has played just 34 minutes in the Premier League this season.

Garnacho was left at home for the 2-0 loss by Galatasaray , with Emery bringing 11 substitutes - including two goalkeepers - rather than the maximum 12.

"When he is not involved in the squad it is because I have to choose with other players as well," said the Villa boss on Friday.

"He has my respect first as a person and second as a player, but he is not involved for this reason.

"But football can change. We are playing matches so I will need players."

Not even making a 12-man bench - what next for Garnacho?

Garnacho has played in just four of Villa's 11 Premier League matches this season and has yet to start across all competitions, coming off the bench for all seven of his appearances.

His last appearance - just a three-minute cameo - came in the 1-1 draw against Fulham on 31 October.

"Alejandro Garnacho is training very well. His attitude is fantastic, very good attitude," Emery added.

"He was struggling at the beginning of the season because he was not fit. Now he is fit and he's training at a good level."

Sources have acknowledged Garnacho was not at the level required and were surprised how off the pace he was when he signed in July.

He initially trained on his own, while his problems were not helped by a head injury suffered in Thailand in pre-season.

"Of course now he, and other players as well, are performing well, they are working well, they understood how we are building the squad," Emery said.

"It's not how it was two months ago when he wasn't fit enough to be playing with the consistency we needed.

"So keep going, keep moving forward as a club, as a team, he himself as a player and we will see it."

Garnacho's move to Villa will become permanent for £43m at the end of the season should certain criteria be met, but there are concerns his time at the club could become similar to that of Harvey Elliot , who played just nine times last season after arriving on loan from Liverpool .

Fifa rules allow players to play for two clubs in a season - or three if they move to a team whose season overlaps like the Major League Soccer - meaning Garnacho could feature for another team, unlike Elliott as he had already played for Liverpool and Villa.

However, Emery said he was not thinking about the upcoming January transfer window as he added: "It is November, of course there is a transfer window in January, but we are not thinking about the transfer window in January. Me especially."

Analysis: Situation could leave players & clubs thinking twice on loan moves

Does this damage Villa after Elliott lost a year of his career last season?

There was already talk in the game of how players could be fearful it could happen to them - and that caution may increase with Garnacho's situation.

Having happened twice in two seasons it would also leave clubs with second thoughts too given the players are their assets.

Garnacho has managed just 95 minutes across all competitions, having joined Villa to revive a faltering career after an inconsistent first season at Chelsea .

Head of football operations Damian Vidagany was unrepentant when asked about the winger at a fans' forum on Thursday, with Emery's trusted lieutenant fiercely backing the manager's judgement call.

Villa, though, arguably need a player like Garnacho - who can produce moments of magic like his stunning goal for Manchester United against Everton in 2023 - having failed to score in four of their last six winless games.

Emery wanted a pacy winger in the summer and the Argentine had been on their wanted list all year.

They need some need some creativity, so with Emery, at least publicly, refusing to rule out a January departure there could still be a slim chance of redemption.

articles.standfirst: El delantero del Fulham mantiene su esperanza de triunfar vestido de blanco
articles.summary: El delantero del Fulham mantiene su esperanza de triunfar vestido de blanco
articles.body: Gonzalo García (Madrid, 2004) cambió el Real Madrid por el Fulham el pasado verano... pero sigue mirando de reojo al Santiago Bernabéu. “Intento ver todos los partidos del Madrid, siempre que no coincidan con los míos. La verdad es que llevan un comienzo bastante bueno, así que feliz por ellos”, confiesa el español, internacional sub 21, a 'DAZN'. El deseo de Gonzalo, traspasado a cambio de 40 millones de euros este verano, aunque con opción de recompra, sigue siendo triunfar vestido de blanco. Y no lo oculta: "No te voy a mentir, no es nada fácil. Yo soy madridista, el haber conseguido estar en el primer equipo del Real Madrid y tener la gran suerte de poder formar parte de ese equipo era y sigue siendo un sueño". "Cuando llega el verano y te plantean la posibilidad de tener que salir, obviamente uno se lo piensa bastante”, reconoce antes de desvelar los pormenores de su traspaso: "Me llamó el míster, me llamó Arbeloa, me explicó el proyecto que había aquí en el Fulham y, hablando con él, uno ve la gran ambición que hay en todo el proyecto, de jugar en la Premier League. Al haber hablado con Álvaro, todo se hizo un poquito más fácil". La adaptación a la Premier League no está siendo fácil: "Es un cambio de estilo de juego, más físico, todo es un poquito distinto a España, pero de momento estoy contento y adaptándome poco a poco”. Marcó en el debut frente al Chelsea (2-3) y, desde entonces, no ha vuelto a marcar en Liga. Sí 'mojó' en Copa de la Liga frente al Wimbledon (3-0). “El cambio es bastante grande, pero creo que vengo muy bien preparado. Llevo doce años jugando en el Real Madrid, uno en el primer equipo y otros once en la cantera, y creo que no hay mejor sitio para aprender y criarse dentro del mundo del fútbol que La Fábrica”, apostilla. Gonzalo no se rinde.

articles.title: España se medirá a Uzbekistán en dieciseisavos del Mundial
articles.standfirst: Los de Cubillo clasificaron como mejor selección a la fase eliminatoria y se enfrentarán a la peor mejor tercera el próximo lunes
articles.summary: Los de Cubillo clasificaron como mejor selección a la fase eliminatoria y se enfrentarán a la peor mejor tercera el próximo lunes
articles.body: Los 15 goles ante Fiyi tenían un premio escondido. Y España acaba de descubrirlo. La selección de David Cubillo se enfrentará el próximo lunes (16.30 horas) a Uzbekistán en los dieciseisavos de final del Mundial Sub-17, después de cerrar una fase de grupos prácticamente perfecta. Tres victorias, 22 goles a favor y ninguno en contra. Unos números que han convertido a España en la mejor primera de las doce selecciones que encabezaron sus respectivos grupos y que le permitirán medirse al rival con peor rendimiento entre los terceros clasificados. Un cruce, sobre el papel, favorable para una generación que todavía no ha encontrado demasiada resistencia en Catar. La explicación está en el nuevo formato que FIFA estrenó en 2025, coincidiendo con la ampliación del campeonato a 48 selecciones. Los doce primeros de grupo, los doce segundos y los ocho mejores terceros acceden a dieciseisavos, pero los enfrentamientos ya no dependen de un cuadro tradicional establecido por grupos. Ahora se ordenan según el rendimiento durante la primera fase. Los ocho mejores primeros se enfrentan a los ocho terceros clasificados, de manera que el primero juega contra el peor y así sucesivamente. Los otros cuatro campeones se miden a los cuatro segundos peor clasificados, mientras los ocho subcampeones restantes se enfrentan entre sí. Un sistema que premia cada victoria y concede especial importancia a la diferencia de goles cuando los equipos igualan a puntos. Y ahí España no ha tenido rival. Los de Cubillo han terminado con nueve puntos y una diferencia de +22, una cifra que les ha permitido superar al resto de campeones de grupo. En el extremo contrario aparece Uzbekistán, que consiguió el último billete reservado a los terceros. El combinado asiático cayó ante Costa de Marfil (1-2) e Italia (1-3), pero su victoria frente a Jamaica (6-2) le permitió sumar tres puntos y una diferencia de goles de +1, suficiente para mantenerse entre los 32 supervivientes. No obstante, su clasificación tampoco debe ocultar sus antecedentes. Uzbekistán se proclamó campeona de Asia Sub-17 en 2025 y llega a Catar después de consolidar su crecimiento en las categorías inferiores. Además, España conoce bien a su próximo adversario. Ambas selecciones se enfrentaron el pasado 27 de agosto en un amistoso de preparación disputado en El Albir, que terminó con victoria española por 3-0. Un precedente favorable para los de Cubillo, aunque ahora la exigencia será distinta. El Mundial entra en su fase decisiva y ya no habrá margen para corregir errores: una derrota supondrá regresar a casa. El cuadro también ha quedado definido. España avanzará por la mitad izquierda, donde se enfrentaría en octavos al vencedor del Irlanda-Costa de Marfil. En unos hipotéticos cuartos aparecería el superviviente de los cruces Croacia-Uruguay y México-Argentina. Por ese mismo lado también avanzan Mali, República Dominicana, Venezuela, Argelia, Grecia, Ecuador, Australia y Senegal, posibles rivales únicamente a partir de semifinales. En el lado opuesto quedan potencias como Francia, Italia, Brasil y Marruecos, a las que los de Cubillo solo podrían encontrarse en una hipotética final.
