articles.title: MAC Title Game Scenarios for Toledo, Ohio, Buffalo, WMU, Miami
articles.summary: The Mid-American Conference has a tendency in recent seasons to come down to the wire, and that’s certainly the case as the 2026 MAC campaign heads toward it...
articles.body:
The Mid-American Conference has a tendency in recent seasons to come down to the wire, and that's certainly the case as the 2026 MAC campaign heads toward its conclusion.

Two teams will meet in the MAC championship game, except neither of the conference title game participants have been decided yet. Toledo, Ohio, Buffalo, Western Michigan and Miami (Ohio) can all still make it to Ford Field in a week's time to play for a conference championship.

That creates some fascinating scenarios in the final couple days of the regular season, with MACtion scheduled for both Friday and Saturday following Thanksgiving.

Here's what you need to know about each team's scenarios to make it to Detroit.

Buffalo gets in with one result and one result only.

If the Bulls beat Akron, they will play for a conference title.

Buffalo would play Toledo if the Rockets win their matchup with Ohio, but they'd play the Bobcats if OU wins that game.

The Bobcats are into the title game with one result and one result only.

If Ohio beats Toledo, they are into the MAC title game.

They could then have potential matchups with Buffalo, WMU, Miami or even Toledo again depending on other results.

The Rockets can make the championship game in two different ways.

The first is if they beat Ohio on Friday. That puts Toledo in for sure.

The second is if Toledo loses but then gets an Akron win over Buffalo and a Ball State win over Central Michigan. In that scenario, Toledo would rematch with Ohio in a week.

If Toledo wins and Buffalo wins, it'll be Rockets-Bulls in Detroit. If Akron upsets Buffalo and Toledo beats Ohio, then it's Toledo-WMU.

Western Michigan MAC Title Game Scenarios

The Broncos don't control their own destiny here. They have two ways to get in, but after the loss to Miami earlier this week, both paths are out of WMU's control.

One scenario has WMU in the title game if Akron beats Buffalo and Toledo beats Ohio.

The other scenario gets Western Michigan in if Akron beats Buffalo and Ohio beats Toledo and CMU beats Ball State and Bowling Green beats UMass.

Miami kept its hopes alive with a win over Western Michigan earlier this week. They need lots of help now.

The RedHawks need all four of these results:

If all four of those things happen, Miami would play Ohio for the MAC title.

articles.title: Urban Meyer Challenges Lincoln Riley to Fix USC’s Biggest Problems as Frustrations Grow: “Quit The Stupid Penalties”
articles.summary: USC has spent much of 2026 looking like a team with enough talent to beat almost anyone. Yet the Trojans have found ways to make life harder for themselves.
articles.body:
USC has spent much of 2026 looking like a team with enough talent to beat almost anyone. Yet the Trojans have found ways to make life harder for themselves.

A costly penalty, a defensive lapse, or a flat performance on the road has repeatedly interrupted their progress. With three losses already, Urban Meyer believes Lincoln Riley needs to spend more time running the entire program.

"USC's probably right behind Oregon as far as talent," Urban Meyer said on his November 24 Triple Option podcast. "Now, they don't always play that way, but USC, if they get—and that's why they got to keep him.

"I don't think they should move on from Riley. Keep Lincoln Riley, hire an offensive coordinator."

Instead of firing the head coach, Meyer argued, Riley needs to attend defensive and special teams meetings, address the penalties, and stop allowing the demands of the offense to consume his working day.

"He's got to go sit in defensive meetings. He's got to go sit in the special teams meetings. He's got to quit the stupid penalties. He's got to do the head coach thing," Urban Meyer added.

The Trojans enter the final week of the regular season at 8-3, with a 5-3 record in Big Ten play. They have scored 30.9 points per game and averaged 422.4 yards of offense through 11 games.

Those numbers give Meyer a reasonable basis for his belief that USC has the personnel to compete with the country's better teams. There have been results to support that view, too.

USC beat Ohio State 30-18 on October 31, handing the Buckeyes one of their biggest setbacks of the season. The Trojans also opened with four consecutive wins and reached 7-2 before their November trip to Indiana.

But the losses have exposed how quickly things can unravel. Oregon beat USC 41-27 at the Coliseum on September 26. Wisconsin then handed the Trojans a 24-7 defeat on October 24, holding them to just one touchdown.

Indiana added another setback with a 27-13 win on November 14. So, Meyer's complaint about discipline has numbers behind it.

USC had been penalized 70 times for 607 yards through 11 games, an average of 6.36 penalties and 55.2 yards per contest. Opponents had been flagged 62 times for 503 yards over the same stretch.

That is not the only problem on the stat sheet, but it is an avoidable cost for a team trying to close the gap with Oregon and the Big Ten's leading programs. Riley has already acknowledged that USC's mistakes have hurt it.

"We just had too many mistakes. We played hard. I thought we played physical," Lincoln Riley said after the IU game. "I thought we were really resilient throughout the game. …We're very disappointed to not get it done."

Meyer, though, has raised the play-calling issue before. On November 20, he argued that Lincoln Riley should bring in someone to handle that responsibility so he could concentrate on the wider demands of the job.

The former Ohio State head coach described modern play-calling as a full-time task, one that can leave a head coach too occupied with the next offensive call to keep track of the entire team.

That does not necessarily mean Riley has to stop being an offensive coach and lose his QB whisperer identity. It means he cannot let that part of his job crowd out everything else.

USC's final regular-season game is against UCLA on November 28 at the Rose Bowl. The Trojans will enter at 8-3, while the rivalry matchup gives Riley one more chance to finish the season with a statement win.

Still, in the past few days, talks about Riley's future at USC have taken a different turn. The focus has moved away from whether the school would fire him and toward the possibility of both sides agreeing to part ways.

USC could face a buyout bill of roughly $70 million if it dismissed Riley outright, making a negotiated exit a more realistic option. So, when TCU let Sonny Dykes go on November 22, Bruce Feldman of The Athletic quickly brought Riley's name into the conversation.

He called the USC head coach an intriguing option for the Fort Worth job and raised the possibility that Riley might be ready to leave Los Angeles after five seasons that have fallen short of expectations.

Pete Nakos of On3 also put Riley's name forward as a possibility for TCU, along with UTSA head coach Jeff Traylor and LSU assistants Charlie Weis Jr. and Blake Baker.

Nakos suggested Riley could look at jobs in Texas, including TCU and Baylor, if USC falls short of the 12-team CFP and the head coach and university agree to go their separate ways. Despite that, Riley still has good reasons to stay.

USC has plenty of young talent coming through the door, much of it brought in under Lincoln Riley. The Trojans finished with the No. 1 recruiting class in the country in 2026, signing 35 players. Twenty came from California.

That group has already been given important jobs. Riley put five true freshmen in the starting lineup for the season opener: five-star edge rusher Luke Wafle, top-ranked tight end Mark Bowman, cornerback Elbert Hill, and wide receivers Trent Mosley and Kayden Dixon-Wyatt.

USC also made several major changes, all with Riley still in charge. The school hired Chad Bowden as general manager to overhaul its recruiting and financial operations, then brought in veteran coach Gary Patterson to run the defense in 2026.

Letting Riley go now would leave USC starting over with a new leadership setup, just as the roster is packed with young players and the changes have barely had time to take hold.

Moreover, the program would be taking a big chance by moving on from a 43-year-old coach who has delivered three Heisman winners, three No. 1 overall NFL Draft picks, and three College Football Playoff appearances.

If the Trojans do not have a clear successor ready to take over, firing Riley could leave them in a worse position. They might get rid of the frustration surrounding the program now, only to spend the next few years trying to build it back up.

articles.title: Hansi Flick delighted with Barcelona heavyweight’s performance in makeshift role
articles.summary: According to MARCA, Hansi Flick has been left delighted with Barcelona midfielder Frenkie de Jong’s performances in a makeshift centre-back role in recent ma...
articles.body:
According to MARCA , Hansi Flick has been left delighted with Barcelona midfielder Frenkie de Jong's performances in a makeshift centre-back role in recent matches.

Having first deployed the Dutchman as a central defender against Alaves, the manager repeated the tactic over the past week against Villarreal and Sabah FK, and the 29-year-old has passed the tests with flying colours.

De Jong gives Flick an additional defensive option

De Jong's deployment in defence was not part of the original plan for this season. However, Flick has now used him in the position in three of his six appearances this campaign, and the midfielder has responded without complaint

His latest display against Sabah was particularly striking, as he combined composure on the ball with an awareness of the defensive responsibilities required of him.

Impressing at centre-back. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

Flick had already made clear how much he appreciates De Jong's attitude ahead of the Sabah fixture.

The Barcelona manager explained that the midfielder had offered to play in any position required by the team, even though he considers the Netherlands star one of the best midfielders in the world.

De Jong, for his part, has never hidden that he prefers to play in his natural position in midfield, but has also admitted that he is prepared to step in wherever the team needed him.

Against Sabah, Flick once again trusted De Jong at the heart of the defence, with Gerard Martin alongside him and Pau Cubarsi given a rest.

Flick pleased with De Jong's performances. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

The Dutchman effectively operated as a libero , helping Barcelona build from the back, carrying the ball forward and stepping across to cover spaces whenever his defensive partners needed support.

The numbers behind his performance were exceptional . Across 64 minutes on the pitch, De Jong completed all 69 passes he attempted, recording 18 successful passes in the opposition half and another 51 in his own half.

De Jong's contribution was not limited to possession as he also stopped a Sabah counter-attack down the left with great authority, made four recoveries and was not dribbled past once.

For a player whose natural position remains in the middle of the pitch, adapting so comfortably to a new role is no small achievement. And the manager has been left impressed by how well he has taken to his new role.

articles.title: Notre Dame Football: Syracuse Orange Q&A with Troy Nunes Is An Absolute Magician
articles.summary: We went into the enemy orchard to find out more about what to expect when Notre Dame takes on Syracuse.
articles.body:
Folks, it's been a crazy week of holiday festivities and family time, so I'm going to keep this intro short and sweet — your 10-1, 4th-ranked Notre Dame Fighting Irish football team will play their regular season finale on Saturday in Syracuse, New York, taking on a 5-6 Syracuse Orange squad with a 2nd Playoff bid in 3 seasons on the line.

So, I reached out to our dear, dear friends over at Troy Nunes Is An Absolute Magician , SB Nation's go-to source for all things Syracuse Orange. Tanner Jace was kind enough to answer various questions about Fran Brown, the Orange offense and defense, Otto the Orange and what he would bring to Thanksgiving, some classic alumni power rankings, and more!

Let's dive right in and see what he had to say about this final matchup before (hopefully) the Irish turn their attention to the Playoff.

1. After a hot start in his first season in 2024 with a 10-3 season and Holiday Bowl victory, Fran Brown is 8-15 since. How are Orange fans feeling about their head coach and where the Syracuse program is heading? Do you think he's the right coach to get them back toward the top of the ACC and competing for a Playoff spot in the expanded 24-team field?

Tanner Jace, Troy Nunes Is An Absolute Magician : The fanbase is 50/50, some of the fanbase will give him a pass due to the QB issues in years 2 and 3, He learned from his mistake last year and went and got two back ups to Angeli that can play and that has come to fruition. But there is a part of the fanbase that is not happy with how inconsistent the team is this year, the young core that he has, really did mature during the middle part of the season along as a coach himself. I think a lot of the fanbase based on the team and schedule would have said the ceiling for this team was 7-5 and the floor was 5-7.

In terms of the future, Fran has done things to help prepare the program for the future, he has a young core of guys that continue to get better, plus he still recruits at a level that the 315 has not seen in 20 plus years, To possibly have 3 straight years of top 50 classes is something that many fans in Syracuse would not of seen coming. With that said and the expansion of the playoff, there is a real shot that if he can get his core back next year and add talent that compliments what he has there is a strong shot that the Orange are competing high in the ACC and are competing for a spot in the 24 team playoff.

2. Whom can Irish fans expect to see under center for Syracuse on Saturday? Are we unfortunately going to once again miss a potential Steve "Peanut Butter" Angeli revenge game? Whomever you expect to start, how have they looked this year and how do you feel they'll fare against a tough Notre Dame defense?

Tanner Jace, Troy Nunes Is An Absolute Magician : Sadly we will all miss out on the Steve Angeli revenge game. The former 5 Star Malachi Nelson is expected to go this week. He, along with most of the Quarterbacks in the room have dealt with injuries. Nelson stepped in after Amari Odom went out with injury, Nelson has done a good job of fitting into the offense, he said during fall camp that this is the most confidence he has felt in his entire college career. Nelson has cut down on the turnovers, something he struggled with at UTSA last season, when he is out on the field he has continued the constant air raid offense that Syracuse has.

In terms of how he fairs against the Irish Defense, the pressure will get to him and he will have to be quick with his decision making. My biggest worry for Nelson is him playing the entire 60 minutes, He has not gone bell to bell all year in his 3 major appearances. He left the Virginia game with a shoulder issue, and left the Louisville and Boston College game due to an ankle issue that has bothered him his season.

3. What skill position players should Irish fans be aware of/afraid of on this Syracuse offense? And how has the Orange offensive line looked — will they be able to get a push and/or prevent pressure from the Irish d-line?

Tanner Jace, Troy Nunes Is An Absolute Magician : The Skill positions by far that ND fans should be aware of are the Wide Receivers, Umari Hatcher is a Top 5 WR in the country this year and you can argue top 3, he trials Jeremiah Smith and Jesse Lagree in receiving yards this season and Top 15 in Receiving Touchdowns with 9. The Freshman Calvin Russell, has been a really nice compliment for Hatcher, his break out game North Carolina in the overtime win where he 8 Catches for 87 Yards and the Game tying touchdown, since then the highest rated recruit in the program's history has only gotten better with his best game against NC State where he set the program record for catches in a game with 17, going for 137 yards and a touchdown in that one as well.

In terms of the Offensive line, The inconsistent play of that group has really hindered the offense. We have not really seen the passing attack and rushing attack work in unison this year. The offense relies on what attack works well in the first few drives and based the rest of the offense around it, the pass protection has been really poor this year and the group really struggles against the blitz and that showed up a lot on film during the Clemson game a few weeks ago. If the O-Line does anything well in this one it's going to be getting a push in the running game.

4. What position groups are strengths and which are weaknesses on the Syracuse defense? Are there any individuals who could make some plays and make things really difficult for CJ Carr and the ND offense?

Tanner Jace, Troy Nunes Is An Absolute Magician : There is a lot of strengths on that Syracuse Defense, But the secondary had been really inconsistent, in the Upset win over SMU, the DB's allowed Kevin Jennings to throw for 351 yards so there is an opportunity for CJ Carr and the ND Offense to hit on big time plays down field and really take the air out of the Dome.

The Defensive line for the Orange could be the x-factor in this one, with the anomaly that has been the last two weeks in opponents rushing the ball, Cuse was holding their opponents to just under 130 rushing yards per game. NC State and Boston College were the first two teams to rush for over 200 yards against Cuse. The four man pass rush has been really consistent this season, and will have to have a big day against on Offensive line that has only allowed CJ Carr to touch the turf four times this season. The Orange pass rush has been known for performing against O-lines that have not allowed many sack, during the SMU game, Syracuse got to Kevin Jennings 6 times in that game, before that Halloween Game, Jennings was sacked less than 10 times.

5. Please power-rank the below Syracuse alumni/former students using whatever criteria you see fit

6. In the 1980s when the Orange mascot was just emerging at Syracuse, Sports Illustrated described it as a "juiced-up, bumbling citrus fruit from which two legs protrude." Would you say that's still an accurate description of Otto the Orange? What kind of inspiration do you think Fran Brown and his program can draw from Otto's original persona?

Tanner Jace, Troy Nunes Is An Absolute Magician : The Juiced Up description is still very much an accurate description. Otto will continue to be the happiest person in every room The Orange is in. The program did take some big inspiration from Otto, when The Orange upset SMU on Halloween Weekend. For the first time ever Otto was the helmet decal during the spooky day, and the team took a big jolt of energy from that.

7. With this being a game just after Thanksgiving, I've gotta toss in a festive question: if I invite Otto the Orange to my family's Thanksgiving gathering, what does he make/bring to contribute to the feast, and how do you think he'll get along with my parents?

Tanner Jace, Troy Nunes Is An Absolute Magician : If Otto was invited to Thanksgiving dinner he's bringing a bowl of Oranges, there is no other way to put it. Otto will get along with anyone, Otto's high energy will be fed from one person to another and will make what is already a great holiday better, and after Thanksgiving dinner, he is a great player to play charades with.

I have the Irish winning this one 35 to 21 , I can definitely see ND scoring more than 40 in this one, the defense for Syracuse has been the highlight of the season, but over the last two weeks have struggled with some consistency especially in the first half of play, the run defense got gashed last week, and if that problem proceeds for the Vince Kehres's defense, Notre Dame can shorten the field and really dominante time of possession against a Cuse team that is top 25 in the country in T.O.P.

Offensively as much as Cuse has had for the most part consistent Quarterback play from all three of its QBs this year, I'm not convinced Syracuse is going to be able to lean on its run game as it has in its biggest wins of the year. I am also not convinced that Malachi Nelson will play the entire game as well, since he has not gone bell to bell in games he has played this season. I think the game will be close at half, SU is playing for another month of practices and a game, I can see Syracuse riding that energy in the first but getting out classed in the second half.

Alrighty folks, I want to give a huge shout-out to Tanner and encourage you all to head on over to the Nunes Magician site to check out some great coverage they've always had going on over there, including a Q&A with yours truly that should be published sometime between now and game time.

I also recommend you give those guys a follow on Twitter for all late-breaking coverage of pregame, during-game, and post-game action for this SHOWDOWN in Syracuse — you won't regret it, right now or during college hoops season.

Otherwise, that's it for now — I need to go eat some more Thanksgiving leftovers and watch a bunch of football for the next couple days. As always, GO IRISH, BEAT ORANGE!!!

articles.title: Charlie Weis Jr. Drawing Interest From Florida State and Oregon
articles.summary: LSU offensive coordinator Charlie Weis Jr. may be looking to establish himself away from Lane Kiffin.
articles.body:
When Charlie Weis Jr. joined LSU from Ole Miss with Lane Kiffin less than a year ago, expectations were that Weis would leave only for a head-coaching or NFL opportunity. Now, according to reports, Weis is a top candidate for the Florida State offensive coordinator job after the Seminoles named Georgia defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann as their new head coach.

According to a source with knowledge of the matter, Weis is not only talking to Florida State but also speaking with Oregon about its offensive coordinator vacancy.

As I speculated on the most recent episode of " Geaux Deep Dive ," Weis' potential interest in Florida State (and now Oregon) would likely be to prove he can run his own offense away from Lane Kiffin. Understandably, with an offensive guru like Kiffin as your head coach, it can be difficult for potential suitors for future head coaching jobs to see past the idea of it being Lane Kiffin's offense and not Charlie Weis Jr.'s.

Weis' history as an offensive coordinator is well documented in my previous piece on The Evolution of the Lane Kiffin Offense , but outside of working under Kiffin, his track record has been questionable at best. In 2020, his first year as the offensive coordinator at USF, the Bulls finished 103rd in the nation with 23.1 points per game, along with 365.3 yards per game, ranked 92nd. It was not much better for Weis and USF in 2021, scoring 23.2 points per game (100th) and gaining 353.5 yards per game (102nd).

In a casual conversation I had with an attorney friend of mine, according to his interpretation, if Weis is to leave LSU before the season ends, the university would be owed $2.5 million. If he were to leave after the conclusion of the season, there would be no buyout.
